questions.stem: When did Nigeria gain her Independence?
questions.explanation: Nigeria became independent from Britain on 1st October 1960.

questions.stem: Democracy means a system of government in which
questions.explanation: Key printed A; correct answer is D because democracy is literally "rule by the people" (government of, by and for the people); majority rule is only one of its operating principles.

questions.stem: A constitution is federal if
options: it provides for a presidential system
the central and component units or authorities are co-ordinate and equal
there is a division of powers between a central and a number of other component authorities
questions.explanation: A federal constitution divides governmental powers between a central government and component (state/regional) governments.

questions.stem: The Executive is
options: the body that executes the policies of government
questions.explanation: The executive arm implements (executes) laws and government policies.

questions.stem: The Judiciary is
options: the body which makes the law
the body which interprets the law
the body which enforces the law
questions.explanation: The judiciary is the arm of government that interprets the law and applies it in settling disputes.

questions.stem: Rights are
options: claims which are natural to men
what are written in the constitution
questions.explanation: Rights are claims or entitlements recognised and protected by law.

questions.topic: Pressure groups: definition, types, functions and modes of operation
questions.stem: Pressure groups are
options: Organization which wants to overthrow the government
organizations which seek to influence the policies of the government
associations of people who share the same ideology
questions.explanation: Pressure groups are organised groups that try to influence government policy in their favour without seeking to control government.

questions.stem: A cabinet system of government is practiced in
questions.explanation: Britain is the classic example of the cabinet (parliamentary) system; the USA is presidential.

questions.stem: The citizen's obligations are
options: duties the individual imposes on himself
what the law requires of the individual
what political parties demand of their members
questions.explanation: Civic obligations are the duties the law requires of every citizen, e.g. paying taxes and obeying the law.

questions.topic: Electoral System: types, advantages and disadvantages of each
questions.stem: An electoral system is the system which governs
options: the appointment of the Pope elections
questions.explanation: An electoral system is the set of rules and procedures governing the conduct of elections.

questions.stem: An unwritten constitution is one which
options: is not subject to judicial review
is made up solely of a set of conventions
questions.explanation: An "unwritten" constitution (e.g. Britain's) is not contained in a single document; parts of it are written in statutes, so it is only partially written.

questions.stem: Delegated legislation is legislation
options: which is not submitted to parliament
made by a minister acting under an Act of Parliament
questions.explanation: Delegated legislation is law made by a body or minister under powers delegated by an Act of the legislature.

questions.stem: Before colonial rule, Yoruba traditional rulers were appointed by
options: the people acting through their representatives
questions.explanation: In pre-colonial Yoruba kingdoms such as Oyo, the Oba was selected by a council of kingmakers (e.g. the Oyomesi).

questions.stem: The first political party properly so-called was formed in Nigeria in
questions.explanation: Herbert Macaulay formed the Nigerian National Democratic Party (NNDP) in 1923 after the elective principle was introduced.

questions.stem: The Loi Cadre, a major factor in the constitutional development of the French colonial territories, was introduced in
questions.explanation: The Loi Cadre (Framework Law) of 1956 introduced universal suffrage and territorial assemblies in French Africa.

questions.stem: The Coussey Commission Report laid the groundwork for the eventual independence of
questions.explanation: The Coussey Committee (1949) recommended the constitutional reforms that led to the 1951 Gold Coast constitution.

questions.stem: The (former) Western Region of Nigeria became internally self-governing in
questions.explanation: The Eastern and Western Regions attained internal self-government in 1957; the North followed in 1959.

questions.stem: The first Pan African conference was held in
questions.explanation: The first Pan-African Conference, organised by Henry Sylvester Williams, met in London in 1900.

questions.topic: Public Commissions Established by the 1979 and Subsequent Constitutions
questions.stem: The Public Service Commission (Nigeria) is responsible for the appointment of all
questions.explanation: The Public (Civil) Service Commission appoints, promotes and disciplines civil servants.

questions.topic: The Judiciary (post-independence): structure, functions and workings
questions.stem: Constitutional cases in Nigeria can only be raised in the first instance in
questions.explanation: Constitutional questions normally begin in the High Courts, with appeals going upward to the Court of Appeal and Supreme Court.

questions.stem: Which of the following would act for the Head of state when he is out of the country?
options: the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court
the Chief of Staff, Supreme Military Headquarters
the Chief of Staff, Air Force
the General Officer Commanding, First Division
questions.explanation: Under the military regime of the time, the Chief of Staff, Supreme Headquarters was the second-in-command and acted for the Head of State.

questions.stem: To raise funds, local governments can levy
questions.explanation: Key printed B; correct answer is D because rates (e.g. tenement/property rates) are the classic local government levy, while income, excise, import and profits taxes belong to higher tiers.

questions.stem: The Economic Commission for Africa is an agency of
questions.explanation: The ECA is one of the regional commissions of the UN Economic and Social Council.

questions.stem: Nigeria is not a member of
options: the Security Council of the UN
questions.explanation: OCAM was an organisation of French-speaking African states; Nigeria never belonged to it.

questions.stem: The primary [function of] political parties is to
questions.explanation: The primary function of political parties is interest aggregation: combining varied demands into policy programmes in order to win power.

questions.stem: The OAU was formed in
questions.explanation: The Organisation of African Unity was founded at Addis Ababa on 25 May 1963.

questions.topic: Election: types and ingredients of a free and fair election
questions.stem: Which of the following is true as a major function of elections?
options: Elections serve the purpose of recruitment of the leaders to office in a modern state
the elections give the people a chance to eliminate opponents who are in office
they are means of testing the popularity of politicians
politicians use elections as tools to deceive the populace
Elections are a means by which politicians keep themselves in power
questions.explanation: Elections are the means by which leaders are recruited into public office in a modern state.

questions.stem: The first Governor General of Nigeria was
options: the late Major General Aguiyi Ironsi
questions.explanation: Lugard became Governor-General of the amalgamated Nigeria in 1914.

questions.stem: The supreme policy-making organ in the Organization of African Unity is
options: the Assembly of Heads of State and Government
questions.explanation: The Assembly of Heads of State and Government was the OAU's supreme organ.

questions.stem: In which of these organs of the United Nations Organization is veto power exercised by some countries
questions.explanation: The five permanent members of the Security Council hold the veto.

questions.topic: Tiers of government and their relationship
questions.stem: In a federal system such as Nigeria the local governments are directly responsible
options: to the federal or central government
to no other level of government
to the federal and state governments
to any level of government which can provide money for its programs
questions.explanation: In Nigeria local governments are created and supervised by the state governments.

questions.stem: The 1946 constitutions in Nigeria and the Gold Coast (Ghana) were the results of
options: pressures from nationalists within the colonies
pressures by the United States of America
pressures from within and from outside these colonies
questions.explanation: The 1946 reforms responded both to nationalist agitation within and post-war external pressures (Atlantic Charter, anti-colonial opinion).

questions.stem: If the rights of the individual are violated or threatened, where can he go for redress?
options: the Ministry for Internal or Home Affairs
questions.explanation: The courts (judiciary) are the guardians of individual rights and provide legal redress.

questions.stem: In the Presidential system of government the president is elected to office by
questions.explanation: In a presidential system the president derives his mandate from a popular election, not from the legislature.

questions.topic: Factors that led to military intervention
questions.stem: The military take over powers from politicians in West African countries
options: when politicians have become corrupt and are reckless in their use of power
when there is a breakdown of law and order in the country
for reasons which touch on the interest of the military
because of the personal ambitions of some politicians
questions.explanation: All the listed reasons have been cited for military coups in West Africa.

questions.topic: Public corporations: definition, types, purpose and functions
questions.stem: By establishing public corporations governments are trying to
options: render crucial services to the public in areas which the civil service cannot effectively handle
make quick profit at the expense of the people
questions.explanation: Public corporations provide essential services that the regular civil service cannot run efficiently.

questions.stem: The constitution of any given country must provide for
options: the rights and duties of the individual
questions.explanation: A constitution allocates powers, defines citizens' rights and duties and establishes the rule of law.

questions.topic: Pressure groups: definition, types, functions and modes of operation
questions.stem: In a modern state, pressure groups find that the most effective way of achieving their purposes is by
options: rigging elections to offices of the state
questions.explanation: Pressure groups seek to influence government decisions (lobbying etc.) rather than capture power.

questions.stem: Which of the following would you consider the most famous among the leaders of nationalist movement in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Herbert Macaulay is widely regarded as the father of Nigerian nationalism.

questions.stem: The idea of collective responsibility in the Executive branch of government means that
options: no single member of the executive can take any responsible decision
a member of the executive has no way out of decisions made in that body
a member of the executive cannot publicly criticize decisions collectively made without first resigning
responsibility within the executive is not unilateral
parliament must ratify executive decisions collectively reached
questions.explanation: Under collective responsibility ministers must defend cabinet decisions publicly or resign.

questions.stem: Indirect Rule as practised by the British in their West African colonies
options: did not attempt to reform existing traditional institutions
was over glorified and expedient nonsense
satisfied neither the rulers nor the ruled
had nothing in common with the reality of French rule in their colonies
meant ruling through existing rulers and attempting to check excesses
questions.explanation: Indirect rule meant governing through traditional rulers under the supervision of British officers.

questions.stem: The French idea of assimilation as applied in their colonies
options: was to make Frenchmen out of African subjects
would have been allowed to produce more Frenchmen in the colonies than in traditional African
recognized real value in traditional African culture and was merely aimed at upgrading it
produced nothing but African puppets in the colonies
was abandoned within a couple of years of its operation
questions.explanation: Assimilation aimed to turn Africans into Frenchmen in culture, language and citizenship.

questions.stem: The most remarkable thing about post-independence political development in the Gambia is
options: that the country has been swallowed up by the much bigger country of Senegal
the relatively untarnished reputation of Sir Dauda Jawara
that without reliance on overwhelming force, the government has remained in power and tolerated opposition
the uniquely robust economy which the government has succeeded in establishing for the country and distributed fairly among its people
questions.explanation: As at 1978, the Gambia was notable for stable multiparty government that tolerated opposition without relying on force.

questions.stem: The dominant idea behind the establishment of the Organization of African Unity is
options: to show the world that Africa can also do what Latin American and Asian countries have done
to provide a framework and opportunities for co-operation on common African problems
to promote economic development of Africa
to have its Secretary-General co-ordinate the foreign policies of member states
questions.explanation: The OAU was set up as a framework for co-operation among African states on common problems.

questions.stem: The new local government reforms in Nigeria
options: seek to establish uniformity in type, purpose and functions of local authorities
make traditional rulers more powerful than ever before
are a waste of time and the federal government's money
promote unity but allow for some diversity in the structure of local governments
would definitely establish clean and efficient governments at the local level
questions.explanation: The 1976 reforms introduced a uniform, single-tier local government system across the country.

questions.stem: The principle of universal adult suffrage refers to
options: the right of all adult people to vote
the legal nature of a constitution
questions.explanation: Universal adult suffrage is the right of all adults to vote irrespective of sex, wealth or education.

questions.topic: Electoral System: types, advantages and disadvantages of each
questions.stem: A constituency
options: is the same as a legislature
is part of the campaign process
is an area or district in which the inhabitants can send a representative to parliament
is an important part of every monarchy
consists of party executives and freewheelers
questions.explanation: Key printed A; correct answer is C because a constituency is an electoral district whose voters elect a representative to the legislature.

questions.stem: The treaty establishing the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) was
options: concluded in Lomé (Togo) in December 1976 after hard and extensive negotiations
designed as the main pillar on which an eventual African common market would be built
the brainchild of Togo and Ghana
signed in Lagos in May 1975 to promote trade and other economic co-operation in the region as a whole
to immediately eliminate tariffs and other barriers to trade among members
questions.explanation: The ECOWAS Treaty was signed in Lagos on 28 May 1975 to promote economic co-operation in West Africa.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a fundamental human right?
questions.explanation: All the listed freedoms are fundamental human rights.

questions.topic: Pressure groups: definition, types, functions and modes of operation
questions.stem: Which of the following are pressure groups?
options: the National Union of Nigerian Students
questions.explanation: Each of these bodies seeks to influence government in the interest of its members.

questions.topic: Pressure groups: definition, types, functions and modes of operation
questions.stem: Pressure groups are really
options: Nuisances which most governments would like to ignore
people with sinister motives who pretend to serve the public interest
Greedy citizens who pursue purely selfish interests
organized bodies which try to influence legislation or government decisions in their favour
organized bodies that are vulnerable to giant companies who use them to promote their interests
questions.explanation: A pressure group is an organised body seeking to influence government decisions in its favour.

questions.stem: The major role of national legislature is to
options: scrutinize and criticize the executive branch
step into political vacuum created by weak executives
make laws for the general welfare of citizens
find ways and means to get money for governments
questions.explanation: The primary function of a legislature is law-making for the good of the people.

questions.stem: A constitution of any country is basically
options: a guide to how the country should be governed
a document stating what the leaders should do
a document stating how to acquire power
questions.explanation: A constitution is the body of rules that guides how a country is governed.

questions.stem: In general constitutions are designed to provide
options: legal remedies for all political problems
Clear alternative to military take-overs of elected governments
general arrangement rules and national objectives within which political activities are conducted
codes of ethic for politicians and punishment for those who break the laws of the land
rigid ideological frameworks for nations that operate the constitutions
questions.explanation: Constitutions set out the general rules and national objectives within which political activity takes place.

questions.stem: The main function of the legislature is
questions.explanation: The legislature is the law-making arm of government.

questions.stem: The franchise is
options: the paper which a voter casts at elections
questions.explanation: Franchise (suffrage) means the right to vote.

questions.stem: A good example of a country with a largely unwritten constitution is
questions.explanation: The British constitution is not codified in a single document.

questions.stem: The term rule of law means
options: everybody is equal before the law
we are being governed by lawyers
questions.explanation: Key printed C; correct answer is D because the rule of law implies the supremacy of law (no one above it) and equality before the law.

questions.stem: Another name for delegated legislation is
questions.explanation: Delegated legislation is also called subordinate, executive or administrative legislation.

questions.stem: Persons legally qualified to vote for parliamentary candidates form
questions.explanation: The electorate is the body of persons qualified to vote in elections.

questions.stem: The distinction between a flexible and a rigid constitution is based on
options: whether it is unitary or federal
questions.explanation: Rigidity or flexibility depends on how difficult the procedure for amending the constitution is.

questions.stem: The primary obligation of citizenship is
options: loyalty to the state and participation in the political process
loyalty to one's school and church
loyalty to one's local government council
voting during local government council elections
questions.explanation: A citizen's first duty is loyalty to the state and participation in its political life.

questions.stem: All Federal systems of government have
options: heads of states who are also heads of government
questions.explanation: Federalism requires a written (and usually rigid) constitution to define the division of powers.

questions.stem: Which of the following governs a state in between meetings of the legislature?
questions.explanation: The executive carries on the day-to-day government of the state at all times.

questions.stem: When a government sincerely strives to make justice and fair treatment the foundations of law and order in its society, we say that the government observes
questions.explanation: Justice and fair treatment under the law are the essence of the rule of law.

questions.stem: The Legislature is
options: the body which administers the law
a body of local government council
the body which interprets the law
questions.explanation: The legislature makes laws.

questions.stem: When we talk about adult male suffrage, we mean
options: all men who pay tax can vote
all adult males who pay tax can vote
questions.explanation: Adult male suffrage extends the vote to all adult men (but not women).

questions.stem: Islam was introduced in Northern Nigeria
options: after the Jihad of Uthman Dan Fodio
by the British in the early 20th century
questions.explanation: Islam reached Kanem-Bornu around the 11th century, long before the 13th century.

questions.stem: Indirect Rule was introduced into Nigeria by
questions.explanation: Lugard introduced indirect rule in Northern Nigeria after 1900.

questions.stem: The French pattern of colonial administration in West Africa
options: was basically the same as the British
had as its primary objective, the development of colonial territories
was based on the principle of assimilation
included the policy of indirect rule
involved the settlement of a very large number of French people in West Africa
questions.explanation: French colonial administration was based on assimilation (later association).

questions.stem: Which of the following did not take part in the early nationalist movement of Nigeria?
options: the Democratic Party of Nigeria and the Cameroons
questions.explanation: The Lagos Weekly Record, NNDP, NYM and West African Pilot were all active in early nationalism; the "Democratic Party of Nigeria and the Cameroons" was not.

questions.stem: In the pre-colonial Igbo political system, which of the following was the most democratic organ of government?
questions.explanation: The village assembly (Oha-na-Eze) in which all adult males could speak was the most democratic organ.

questions.stem: When was the emirate system of government introduced in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Key printed C; correct answer is A because the emirate system was established after Uthman dan Fodio's jihad began in 1804, i.e. in the nineteenth century.

questions.stem: In the organization of British colonial rule in West Africa, which of these was the lowest level of government and administration?
questions.explanation: The District Commissioner/Officer administered the district, the lowest level of colonial administration listed.

questions.stem: The colonial administration in Nigeria was
questions.explanation: Colonial administration was imposed and run by appointed officials without popular consent: it was authoritarian.

questions.stem: The system of Indirect Rule failed in the former Eastern Nigeria primarily because
options: the Chiefs refused to co-operate with colonial officers
of the high incidence of taxation
the colonial officers imposed warrant chiefs on the people
questions.explanation: Igboland had no centralised chieftaincy (a segmentary, fragmented structure), so there were no traditional rulers to rule through.

questions.stem: The three largest political parties in Nigeria between 1951 and 1966 were
options: Northern People's Congress (NPC), Action Group (AG), Northern Elements Progressive Union (NEPU)
United National Independence Party (UNIP), National Council of Nigerian Citizens (NCNC) and NPC
Nigerian Union of Teachers (NUT), AG, NEPU
United Middle Belt Congress (UMBC), NPC and NCNC
questions.explanation: The NCNC, NPC and AG were the three major regional parties of the period.

questions.stem: Which of the following people was one of the founding members of the National Congress of British West Africa?
questions.explanation: Key printed A; correct answer is D because Dr R. Akiwande Savage was among the Nigerian founders of the NCBWA in 1920; Bode Thomas belonged to a later generation.

questions.stem: The Mid-Western Region was created in Nigeria in
questions.explanation: The Mid-West Region was carved out of the Western Region in 1963.

questions.topic: The Judiciary (post-independence): structure, functions and workings
questions.stem: In Nigeria, appellate cases from Courts of Appeal go to
questions.explanation: The Supreme Court is the final court of appeal in Nigeria.

questions.stem: Which is the supreme organ of the OAU?
options: the assembly of the heads of state and government
questions.explanation: Key printed E; correct answer is C because the Assembly of Heads of State and Government was the OAU's supreme organ.

questions.stem: Which UN organ has primary responsibility for the maintenance of World peace and security?
questions.explanation: Key printed C; correct answer is E because the UN Charter (Art. 24) gives the Security Council primary responsibility for international peace and security.

questions.stem: Sir Henry Willink of Britain was the chairman of a commission which investigated one of the following problems of Nigeria in 1958.
questions.explanation: The Willink Commission (1957-58) inquired into the fears of minorities.

questions.stem: The OAU has its headquarters in
questions.explanation: The OAU (now AU) is headquartered in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.

questions.stem: Which of the following countries in West Africa has not experienced military intervention in politics?
questions.explanation: As at 1979, Ivory Coast had not had a coup (its first came in 1999), while the others had.

questions.stem: ECOWAS represents
options: the English-speaking equivalent of the Francophone economic community in West Africa
an attempt to progressively eliminate obstacles to free movement of goods, services and people throughout West Africa
the West African regional arm of the United Nations Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC)
a continent-wide economic dimension of pan-Africanism
a concrete achievement by the Economic Commission for Africa (ECA)
questions.explanation: ECOWAS aims at progressively removing barriers to the free movement of goods, services and persons in West Africa.

questions.stem: In the Oyo traditional political system the Alaafin of Oyo was elected or chosen by a group known as
questions.explanation: The Oyomesi, the council of seven kingmakers, chose the Alaafin.

questions.stem: Colonialism was successfully imposed on West Africa because
options: the colonial people thought colonialism was divinely inspired and therefore readily welcomed the imperial power with open arms
the colonial people believed the white man to be superior to the black man and they were in Africa on a civilizing mission
the colonial people believed they were being liberated from the autocratic rule of the indigenous ruling elite
the colonial people could not withstand the technological superiority of the colonial power
questions.explanation: Key printed C; correct answer is E because colonial rule was imposed largely by force; African states could not match European military technology (e.g. the Maxim gun).

questions.stem: In the history of Nigeria 1914 was the
options: year the British established their rule over Nigeria
beginning of the First World War
year Lugard effected the amalgamation of Nigeria
year of the first election into the legislative council
year the railway system was completed
questions.explanation: Lugard amalgamated the Northern and Southern Protectorates in 1914.

questions.stem: Which of the leaders rejected Charles de Gaulle's Constitutional proposals in 1958?
questions.explanation: Sekou Toure led Guinea to vote "No" in the 1958 referendum and take immediate independence.

questions.stem: The first country in West Africa to become independent was
questions.explanation: Ghana became independent in 1957, the first of the listed colonial territories.

questions.stem: In their deliberations on the Sharia issue, the Constituent Assembly in Nigeria
options: threw out the entire issue from the proposed constitution
accepted the recommendations of the Constitution Drafting Committee (CDC)
United the country over the issue of sharia
accepted the principle of sharia law and justice but modified the provision in the Draft Constitution
through its debate clearly educated the majority of the people of Nigeria on the principles of Sharia law and Justice
questions.explanation: The 1977-78 Constituent Assembly dropped the proposed Federal Sharia Court of Appeal but retained Sharia courts in the states, modifying the draft.

questions.topic: Electoral System: types, advantages and disadvantages of each
questions.stem: An electoral district is
questions.explanation: An electoral district from which a representative is elected is a constituency.

questions.topic: Pressure groups: definition, types, functions and modes of operation
questions.stem: Pressure groups' politics are usually directed to
options: the interests of the Nigerian Medical Association
the goals of the Nigeria Union of Teachers
questions.explanation: Pressure groups pursue the limited, sectional interests of their members.

questions.topic: Relationships among the arms of government
questions.stem: The principle of separation of powers ensures
options: the preservation of the fundamental liberties of the citizens
that all the branches of government have equal powers and functions
that the rights of the ethnic minorities are safeguarded
questions.explanation: By preventing concentration of power, separation of powers protects citizens' liberties.

questions.stem: A democratic system of government is
options: a mass government on behalf of the people
a government that grants absolute freedom to all citizens
a government of the people by the people and for the people
questions.explanation: Abraham Lincoln's classic definition: government of the people, by the people, for the people.

questions.stem: When we talk about the constitution of any given country, we mean
options: the general body of rules and principles controlling the distribution of governmental power
a guidebook containing the functions of trade union movements
a document embodying rules and principles regulating the exercise of government power
a document defining the relations between the rulers and ruled
questions.explanation: A constitution embodies the rules distributing and regulating governmental power and defines rulers' relations with the ruled.

questions.stem: The concept of Indirect Rule in Nigeria is usually associated with
questions.explanation: Key printed E; correct answer is D because Lord Lugard introduced and systematised indirect rule in Nigeria.

questions.stem: A good example of a country which operates a cabinet system of government is
questions.explanation: Britain is the home of the cabinet (Westminster) system.

questions.stem: A presidential system of government is one
options: where the Head of State possesses real power
where the principle of separation of powers is inapplicable
which provides for a ceremonial Head of State
in which the president is not accountable to any one
in which the parliament cannot remove the president from office before the expiration of his term in office
questions.explanation: In a presidential system the president is both head of state and head of government, wielding real executive power.

questions.stem: A constitution is a document
options: which states in written form the basic laws governing a country
which spells out how the president is to be elected
which forms the basis upon which a government rules a given state
which states that the central government is superior to state governments
questions.explanation: A constitution is the fundamental basis on which government rules a state (it need not be wholly written).

questions.stem: The legislative arm of a government is always
questions.explanation: Whatever its name, the legislature is the law-making body.

questions.stem: The Executive is the body that
questions.explanation: The executive implements laws.

questions.topic: Relationships among the arms of government
questions.stem: The principle of separation of powers implies that
options: power is shared by different but co-ordinate organs in the state
power is shared by competing departments in the state
questions.explanation: Separation of powers distributes governmental power among co-ordinate legislative, executive and judicial organs.

questions.stem: The term rule of law is applicable only
options: in states where laws are supreme
if the regime is not military
questions.explanation: The rule of law exists wherever the law is supreme.

questions.stem: Fundamental human rights of citizens are provided for in
questions.explanation: Citizens' fundamental rights are entrenched in the constitutions of their states.

questions.stem: It is the duty of every citizen
options: to participate in the operation feed the nation scheme
to sing the national anthem every day
questions.explanation: Every citizen has the duty to perform his civic responsibilities.

questions.stem: A one party state is a state where
options: there is complete agreement on issues among party members
the ruling party is the only legal one
questions.explanation: In a one-party state only one party is legally permitted.

questions.stem: The term 'franchise' refers to
options: the right to choose representatives to the legislature
questions.explanation: Franchise is the right to vote, i.e. to choose representatives.

questions.stem: The doctrine of the Dual Mandate was put forward to justify
options: the introduction of Islam in Africa
questions.explanation: Lugard's "Dual Mandate in British Tropical Africa" (1922) justified colonial rule as benefiting both Europe and Africa.

questions.stem: Delegated legislation
options: means sharing responsibility between central and local government on a fifty-fifty basis
decentralizes responsibility for law making subject to agreed controls from the center
once permitted is almost impossible to control
decentralizes problems without providing suitable solutions
questions.explanation: Delegated legislation passes law-making power to subordinate bodies while the parent legislature retains control.

questions.topic: Pressure groups: definition, types, functions and modes of operation
questions.stem: The main role of pressure groups is to
options: influence the Legislature and the Executive to make decisions favourable to them
inject emotional and selfish issues into national debates
use all means including bribery to achieve their objectives
assist selected multinational corporations in fulfilling their objectives
questions.explanation: Pressure groups seek to influence legislative and executive decisions in their favour.

questions.stem: Within a democracy, Citizens
options: can use all and any means to overthrow an offensive government
have the right and duty to be involved in the political process
have the duty to eliminate their political opponents
are advised to be eternally vigilant
have the positive right to physically prevent military coups from taking place
questions.explanation: Democratic citizens have both the right and duty to participate in politics.

questions.stem: The concept of Parliamentary Government in Britain is
options: turning into Prime ministerial and Whitehall government in practice
in fact identical with the Presidential system in the USA
supported by a tiny segment of the population
rejected by the aristocracy of that country
questions.explanation: Commentators note that British cabinet government has become prime-ministerial government with strong civil service (Whitehall) influence.

questions.stem: The basic element of the United States Constitution is that
options: it presupposes and relies upon the existence of a highly educated and very articulate electorate
Presidents like Richard Nixon cannot get away with gross abuse of power
it guarantees the enjoyment of equal rights and protection by every citizen
murderers who are found guilty by law courts are executed on electric chairs
it embodies the concept of separation of powers
questions.explanation: The US Constitution is built on the separation of powers with checks and balances.

questions.stem: Which of the following constitutes the political sovereign in a democracy?
questions.explanation: In a democracy political sovereignty resides with the electorate.

questions.stem: The principle of the Separation of powers in the new Constitution of Nigeria is different from that of the USA because
options: traditional rulers can play dominant role
there are two houses of the National Assembly
the President is above the law
the Vice President is not the President of the Senate
the Senate has the power of veto
questions.explanation: Under the 1979 constitution the Senate elected its own President, whereas the US Vice President presides over the Senate.

questions.stem: The five political parties recognized by the Nigerian Federal Electoral Commission (FEDECO) for the 1979 elections were
options: UPN, GNPP, NPN, PRP and NPC
GNPP, PRP, UPN, NPP and NAP
PRP, UPN, MOP, GNPP and NPP
NPN, NPP, UPN, PRP and GNPP
NPP, PRP, GNPP, NPN and NEPU
questions.explanation: FEDECO registered NPN, NPP, UPN, PRP and GNPP in 1978.

questions.stem: The common colonial institutions in British West Africa included
options: the West African Research Council and Gambia Police Force
the West African Universities Commission and West African Joint Admission and Matriculation Board
the West African Currency Board and the West African Airways Corporation
the West African Teachers Association and West African Labour Union
questions.explanation: The West African Currency Board and West African Airways Corporation served all the British West African colonies.

questions.stem: An ideology is essentially
questions.explanation: A political ideology is a set of ideas that guides political action.

questions.stem: In all countries, the roles of law making, and law interpretation revolve respectively on
questions.explanation: The legislature makes laws; the judiciary interprets them.

questions.stem: The (former) Northern Region of Nigeria became internally self-governing in
questions.explanation: The Northern Region attained self-government in March 1959.

questions.stem: The Convention People's Party was a popular political party in
questions.explanation: Kwame Nkrumah founded the CPP in the Gold Coast (Ghana) in 1949.

questions.stem: Which of the following political movements had the greatest impact on Nigerian nationalists before the 1950s?
options: National Congress of British West Africa
questions.explanation: The NCBWA (1920) directly stimulated constitutional reform (the 1922 elective principle) and Nigerian nationalist activity.

questions.stem: The abolition of the indigénat was effected in French colonies in
questions.explanation: The indigénat (arbitrary native penal code) and forced labour were abolished in 1946.

questions.stem: The ratification of the appointment of an Emir in the pre-colonial Fulani Society was done by the
questions.explanation: Emirs were confirmed by the Sultan of Sokoto or the Emir of Gwandu, depending on which half of the caliphate they belonged to.

questions.stem: Sekou Toure is famous for having said
options: that he preferred independence with difficulty than heavy colonial rule
no to de Gaulle's idea of a French community and opting instead for immediate independence for Guinea
seek ye first the political kingdom and all else will follow given right combination of leadership and national ideology
that power tends to corrupt and absolute power corrupts absolutely
questions.explanation: Sekou Toure led Guinea to reject the 1958 French Community proposal and become independent.

questions.stem: Nationalist movements in West Africa
options: began earlier in the French colonies than in the British ones
were given all necessary support by the colonial governors who were liberal at heart
were assisted by indigenous individuals educated in Europe and North America
were in fact encouraged and later led by traditional rulers who had the much-needed foresight and courage
were parochial and did not really influence one another
questions.explanation: Western-educated Africans (e.g. Azikiwe, Nkrumah) led the nationalist movements.

questions.stem: The French policy of Assimilation
options: Enabled Europeans to assimilate and come to terms with African cultural values
produced radical African leaders who were anxious to terminate cordial relationships with France
was aimed at converting Africans into Frenchmen
was the same in theory as the British policy of Indirect Rule
was a device to transfer French technology to Africa
questions.explanation: Assimilation aimed to make Africans French in culture and outlook.

questions.stem: It was through the activities of ... that the Niger area became a British sphere of influence
questions.explanation: Goldie's Royal Niger Company secured the Niger area for Britain before the Berlin Conference and until 1900.

questions.stem: The 1976 local government reforms provide for a ... term of office
questions.explanation: The 1976 reforms fixed a three-year tenure for local government councils.

questions.topic: Finance, control and problems of public corporations
questions.stem: The major problems that confront public corporations in Nigeria include
options: Management problems corruption and ethnic loyalty
excessive government directives and lack of funds
lack of public patronage and excessive competition from the private sector
questions.explanation: Public corporations suffer from mismanagement, corruption, political interference, under-funding, red tape and manpower shortage.

questions.topic: The Judiciary (post-independence): structure, functions and workings
questions.stem: The highest Court in Nigeria is called the
questions.explanation: The Supreme Court is the apex court.

questions.stem: The Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) came into being
options: through the combined efforts of Gambia, Ivory Coast and Liberia
to promote economic growth and development through freer and expanded trade between its members
to enable the sixteen member states surrender their sovereignties to a supranational regional community
to help the poorest countries in the region catch up with the richer ones
to establish mutual defence and security arrangements between members
questions.explanation: ECOWAS was set up to promote economic co-operation and freer trade among members.

questions.stem: Which of the following bodies is the most representative organ of the United Nations Organization?
questions.explanation: All member states are represented equally in the General Assembly.

questions.topic: Public Commissions Established by the 1979 and Subsequent Constitutions
questions.stem: Which of the following bodies in Nigeria performs the function of an Ombudsman?
questions.explanation: The Public Complaints Commission (1975) is Nigeria's ombudsman.

questions.stem: A permanent civil service
questions.explanation: A permanent civil service ensures continuity when governments change.

questions.topic: Pressure groups: definition, types, functions and modes of operation
questions.stem: The main role of pressure groups is to
options: protect the interest of the country against foreign power
resist temptation of gifts made by multi-national companies to influence their political parties
influence legislation in order to benefit their members
questions.explanation: Pressure groups seek to influence legislation and policy for their members' benefit.

questions.stem: The power of British Trade Unions now constitutes
options: a real threat to the Queen and the British Establishment
a threat to the House of Lords
a challenge to the idea of Parliamentary Sovereignty
a menace to the Confederation of British Industries
questions.explanation: By 1981 the strength of British unions was seen as challenging Parliament's sovereign authority over policy.

questions.stem: Collective responsibility means that
options: all ministers are collectively responsible to the prime minister
ministers are collectively responsible to the parliament
no minister may publicly criticize decisions made collectively in cabinet without first resigning
ministers must first clear their public statements on policy matters with the cabinet office before delivering them
ministers must always show a sense of responsibility towards one another
questions.explanation: Collective responsibility binds every minister to cabinet decisions; a dissenting minister must resign.

questions.stem: Under the Presidential system of government in Nigeria
options: there is no formal opposition in the national legislature
the Majority party is that of the President
State governments do not have any powers except those allowed by the Central Government
the personal staff of the President are civil servants
questions.explanation: The 1979 presidential constitution provided no official opposition (no Leader of the Opposition) in the National Assembly.

questions.topic: Relationships among the arms of government
questions.stem: Under the United States Constitution
options: the presidency is clearly superior in practice to the other two branches of government
Black Americans enjoy preferential treatment to compensate for past injustices
no branch of government can function without co-operating with the others
questions.explanation: Checks and balances make each branch dependent on the co-operation of the others.

questions.stem: The British constitution, by being unwritten
options: Encourages the dominance of the Prime Minister
gives room for the development of conventions
enables the queen to do no wrong
questions.explanation: Being uncodified, the British constitution relies heavily on conventions which develop over time.

questions.stem: Constitutions are useful documents because they
options: provide ammunition to different sides in ideological disputes
reward the patriotic and punish traitors
lay down broad guidelines for national political interaction
highlight the procedures for the creation of new states
questions.explanation: Constitutions set broad guidelines for political interaction within a nation.

questions.stem: The Nigerian electoral system gives voting rights to
options: Africans above the age of twenty-one
Nigerian citizens who are 18 years old and above
questions.explanation: Nigerian citizens aged 18 and above may vote.

questions.stem: The inalienable rights of the citizens are best protected through
questions.explanation: An independent judiciary enforces citizens' rights against all, including government.

questions.stem: The primary function of the judiciary is to
questions.explanation: The judiciary interprets laws.

questions.topic: The Legislative (post-independence): structures, functions and workings
questions.stem: The main function of the National Assembly is to
options: fix salaries for all the state governors
pass motions on the welfare of the legislators
direct public attention to the excesses of public officials
condemn the South African government for its policy of apartheid
questions.explanation: The National Assembly is Nigeria's federal law-making body.

questions.topic: The Judiciary (post-independence): structure, functions and workings
questions.stem: The decision of the Supreme Court of Nigeria is
questions.explanation: As the apex court, the Supreme Court's decisions are final.

questions.topic: Relationships among the arms of government
questions.stem: The doctrine of the separation of powers is based on the assumption that
options: those who hold power may encroach on the liberties of the powerless
power corrupts and absolute power corrupts absolutely
questions.explanation: Separation of powers rests on the fear that concentrated power corrupts and endangers liberty.

questions.stem: Constitutions have been classified as rigid or as flexible according to
options: whether they were written or unwritten
whether they were popular or unpopular
the relative ease or difficulty of the writing process
the relative ease or difficulty of the amending process
questions.explanation: Rigidity or flexibility depends on the amendment procedure.

questions.stem: Lord Lugard is widely regarded as
options: The most imaginative governor in the British colonies
The originator of the durbar ceremony in Northern Nigeria
The best friend which Southern Nigerian nationalist leaders ever had
questions.explanation: Lugard is called the father (architect) of indirect rule.

questions.stem: Nationalism in West Africa aimed at
options: working out an alliance with the colonial regimes
bringing all the educated elite together
the attainment of political independence from Britain
the attainment of political independence from the colonizers
founding an economic union like ECOWAS
questions.explanation: West African nationalism (British and French colonies alike) sought independence from the colonial powers.

questions.stem: The Nigerian Youth Movement was founded in
questions.explanation: Key printed C; correct answer is D because the Lagos Youth Movement (1934) was renamed the Nigerian Youth Movement in 1936.

questions.stem: The Richards Constitution in Nigeria provided for the
options: unification of the territories ruled by Britain in West Africa
division of Nigeria into three administrative units
replacement of the colonial governor within Nigeria
questions.explanation: The 1946 Richards Constitution introduced regionalism, creating the Northern, Western and Eastern regional councils.

questions.stem: One important aspect of the Lyttleton Constitution was the
options: abolition of the regional Houses of Assembly
declaration that Nigeria would be independent in 1960
enormous powers given to the colonial governors
creation of the post of a Federal Prime Minister
questions.explanation: The 1954 Lyttleton Constitution made Nigeria a true federation with greater regional autonomy.

questions.stem: The Guggisberg Constitution of 1925 in Ghana
options: strengthened the authority of natural rulers
weakened the authority of natural rulers
enhanced the status of the educated elite
abolished the post of colonial governor
made no provision for unofficial members in the legislative Council
questions.explanation: The 1925 Guggisberg constitution created Provincial Councils of Chiefs, strengthening traditional rulers.

questions.stem: The three well-known national leaders in Nigeria between 1948 and 1966 were
options: Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe, Chief Obafemi Awolowo and Alhaji Ahmadu Bello
Lord Lugard, Sir Arthur Richards and Sir John Macpherson
Herbert Macaulay, Ernest Ikoli and Okokon Ndem
Alhaji Isa Kaita, Dr K.O. Mbadiwe and Chief S.L. Akintola
Mallam Aminu Kano, Sir Mobolaji Bank-Anthony and J.S. Tarka
questions.explanation: Azikiwe (NCNC), Awolowo (AG) and Ahmadu Bello (NPC) dominated the period.

questions.stem: The four British colonial territories in West Africa were
options: Ivory Coast, Gambia, Nigeria and Senegal
Nigeria, Ghana, Gambia and Sierra Leone
Senegal, Sierra Leone, Nigeria and Ghana
questions.explanation: Britain ruled Nigeria, Gold Coast (Ghana), Gambia and Sierra Leone.

questions.stem: The system of Indirect Rule in Nigeria
options: enhanced the attainment of political Independence
suited the traditional political systems of Eastern Nigeria
questions.explanation: By empowering traditional rulers and excluding the educated elite, indirect rule slowed nationalism.

questions.stem: The main goals of colonial administration in Nigeria were the
options: industrialization and expansion of the economy
preservation and protection of traditional heritage
maintenance of law and order and exploitation of the national wealth
introduction and promotion of human rights
questions.explanation: Colonial rule aimed at keeping order and exploiting the colony's resources.

questions.stem: The 1958 Constitutional Conferences responded to the fears of minorities by recommending the
options: creation of the office of Inspector-General of Police
questions.explanation: Following the Willink report, fundamental human rights were entrenched in the constitution instead of creating new states.

questions.stem: The breakdown of the Macpherson Constitution was partly caused by the crisis within the
options: National Council of Nigeria and the Cameroons
questions.explanation: The 1953 crisis in the NCNC (Eastern House of Assembly deadlock) contributed to the collapse of the Macpherson Constitution.

questions.topic: Comparison of British and French colonial administration
questions.stem: Cultural assimilation was a feature of
options: King Leopold's rule in the Congo
questions.explanation: Both the French and the Portuguese (assimilado system) practised assimilation.

questions.topic: The Legislative (post-independence): structures, functions and workings
questions.stem: In order to qualify for membership of the House of Representatives in Nigeria, a citizen must have attained the age of
questions.explanation: Under the 1979 Constitution in force in 1981, a member of the House of Representatives had to be at least 30 years old.

questions.stem: Which former Head of State of Ghana was executed during the rule of the Armed Forces Revolutionary Council (AFRC)?
questions.explanation: In June 1979 the AFRC executed former heads of state Afrifa, Acheampong and Akuffo.

questions.stem: Where is the Headquarters of the Fund of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS)?
questions.explanation: The ECOWAS Fund for Co-operation, Compensation and Development was sited in Lomé, Togo.

questions.topic: The Executive (post-independence): structure, functions and workings
questions.stem: The President of Nigeria
options: has a tenure of seven years
has to be elected every four years
has a tenure of five years
questions.explanation: Under the 1979 Constitution the President was elected for a four-year term.

questions.stem: President Shehu Shagari was elected
questions.explanation: Shagari was declared winner of the 1979 presidential election at the first ballot (upheld in Awolowo v. Shagari), so no run-off or electoral college was needed.

questions.stem: The Organization of African Unity was established for the main purpose of
options: opposing imperialism in all its forms and manifestations
Protecting the human rights of all Africans wherever they may live
encouraging cooperation and unity among African States
questions.explanation: The OAU's central purpose was to promote unity and co-operation among African states.

questions.stem: Once a country changes from military to civilian rule, future military rule becomes
options: question only of the wishes of senior military officers
difficult if the civilian regime pursues popular and widely beneficial policies
questions.explanation: Popular, legitimate civilian government reduces the excuses for military intervention.

questions.stem: The headquarters of registered political parties in Nigeria must be located in
options: the state where most of their supporters come from
the Northern and Southern parts of Nigeria
questions.explanation: The 1979 Constitution required a registered party's headquarters to be in the federal capital.

questions.topic: The Judiciary (post-independence): structure, functions and workings
questions.stem: The head of the Judiciary in every state of the Federal Republic of Nigeria is called
questions.explanation: Key printed A; correct answer is E because the head of a state judiciary is the Chief Judge of the State; Chief Justice is the title of the head of the federal judiciary.

questions.stem: With the adoption of the presidential system of government, Nigeria ceased to
options: be a member of the Commonwealth
have different persons as Head of State and Government
operate the principle of separation of powers
questions.explanation: In the presidential system the President combines the roles of head of state and head of government.

questions.topic: Public corporations: definition, types, purpose and functions
questions.stem: Public corporations are set up to
options: cater for those businesses that cannot be left entirely to private enterprise
enhance the prestige of the government
questions.explanation: Public corporations provide essential services that should not be left entirely to private enterprise.

questions.stem: The Commonwealth is an organization
options: of all states formerly in the British Empire
of most of the states in the defunct British Empire
of all English-speaking countries of the world
of only Asian and African countries
which effectively coordinates the policies of its members
questions.explanation: Most, but not all, former British territories belong to the Commonwealth.

questions.topic: The Legislative (post-independence): structures, functions and workings
questions.stem: The highest legislative body in Nigeria is the
questions.explanation: The National Assembly (Senate and House of Representatives together) is the highest legislative body.

questions.topic: Tiers of government and their relationship
questions.stem: Under the constitution of the Second Federal Republic of Nigeria, statutory allocation of revenue to local government councils is the responsibility of the
questions.explanation: The 1979 Constitution empowered the National Assembly to prescribe allocations from the Federation Account to local governments.

questions.stem: In 1964, the National Council of Nigerian Citizens and the Action Group formed the
questions.explanation: The NCNC and AG formed the UPGA for the 1964 federal elections.

questions.stem: The local government reforms of 1976 in Nigeria were designed to
questions.explanation: The 1976 reforms aimed at all these objectives.

questions.stem: The use of the veto in the Security Council is
options: the prerogative of all its members
the exclusive right of the two superpowers the U.S.S.R. and the U.S
questions.explanation: Only the five permanent members have the veto.

questions.stem: Which pair of West African countries influenced each other's post-independence political development most?
questions.explanation: Nigeria and Ghana, the leading former British West African colonies, strongly influenced each other's politics.

questions.stem: Universal Suffrage means
options: giving voting right to women above the age of 21
citizens who understand why they vote
the right of qualified adults to vote
questions.explanation: Universal suffrage is the right of all qualified adult citizens to vote, regardless of sex, property, religion or literacy.

questions.stem: In the Parliamentary System of government executive powers are vested in
options: a few powerful men in the country
questions.explanation: In a parliamentary system real executive power is exercised by the Prime Minister and the Cabinet.

questions.stem: In a federal system, powers that are allocated to both Central and State governments are called
questions.explanation: Concurrent powers are those on which both the central and state governments can legislate.

questions.stem: In a democracy, political power is exercised by
questions.explanation: Democracy is government by the people, in practice through the will of the majority.

questions.topic: Election: types and ingredients of a free and fair election
questions.stem: The purpose of registration before elections is to
options: know the total population of a country
know the names of all taxable adults
know the number of people that support each political party
identify citizens and non-citizens of a state
questions.explanation: Voter registration produces a register of eligible voters, which helps prevent multiple or fraudulent voting.

questions.stem: In a parliamentary system of government the head of government is usually
questions.explanation: The Prime Minister heads the government in a parliamentary system, while the head of state is ceremonial.

questions.topic: The Executive (post-independence): structure, functions and workings
questions.stem: In the presidential system in Nigeria the Chief Executive remains in office for
options: as long as he enjoys popular support
questions.explanation: The President under the 1979 Constitution was elected for a fixed term of four years.

questions.stem: The idea of democracy as a system of government was inherited from
questions.explanation: Democracy originated in the ancient Greek city-states, notably Athens.

questions.stem: We say that a constitution is rigid if
options: it has no chapter on human rights
the process of changing it is too cumbersome
questions.explanation: A rigid constitution requires a special, difficult procedure for amendment.

questions.stem: All of the following are obligations of citizens except
questions.explanation: Giving alms is a private act of charity, not a civic obligation.

questions.stem: Anonymity of the civil servant means that civil servants must
options: not receive the credit or blame for any good or bad policy
questions.explanation: Under anonymity, ministers take public credit or blame for policies; civil servants remain faceless.

questions.stem: A court order directing a detainee to be brought to court is called
questions.explanation: Key printed B; correct answer is D because the writ of habeas corpus orders that a detained person be produced in court so the legality of the detention can be tested.

questions.stem: To say that a country has a multi-party system means that
options: there are only two political parties in existence
only two parties can contest elections
the constitution recognizes more than one party
more than one party should form the government at a time
manifestoes of all political parties are the same
questions.explanation: A multi-party system is one in which the constitution permits several parties to exist and compete.

questions.topic: Pressure groups: definition, types, functions and modes of operation
questions.stem: Pressure groups are important because they
options: manage political crisis for their members
represent groups who may otherwise be ignored
are not interested in the welfare of the state
questions.explanation: Pressure groups articulate the interests of sections of society that might otherwise go unheard.

questions.topic: Electoral System: types, advantages and disadvantages of each
questions.stem: A constituency is the same as
options: a region in a federal system of government
any large town where people vote
questions.explanation: A constituency is an electoral district that elects a representative to the legislature.

questions.stem: In the British parliamentary system, if parliament passes a vote of no confidence on the government, the Prime Minister
options: can ask the Queen to resign
can dismiss some top civil servants
and his cabinet may feel obliged to resign
questions.explanation: By convention a government defeated on a vote of no confidence resigns (or seeks a dissolution).

questions.topic: Electoral System: types, advantages and disadvantages of each
questions.stem: Which of these is NOT a method of election?
questions.explanation: Co-option is appointment of a member by an existing body, not an election by voters.

questions.stem: An unwritten constitution is the one where
options: no part of the constitution is ever written down
the whole constitution is not contained in any one document
the constitution is based on the wishes of the prime minister
the constitution can be amended by a simple majority
questions.explanation: An unwritten constitution is not codified in a single document, though parts of it are written in statutes.

questions.stem: A body of people and institutions that make and enforce laws for a particular society is called
questions.explanation: Government is the machinery of persons and institutions that make, execute and interpret laws for the state.

questions.stem: A constitution refers to
options: basic rules for conducting the affairs of any organization
the doctrine that the power of government must be limited
questions.explanation: A constitution is the body of fundamental rules by which an organization or state is governed.

questions.stem: The idea of putting everyone under two levels of government at the same time is called
questions.explanation: Under federalism every citizen is subject to both the central and the state (regional) governments.

questions.stem: One of the fundamental features of capitalism is
options: that the major factors of production are privately owned
the predominance of the public sector in the economy
the elimination of all forms of competition
questions.explanation: Capitalism is based on private ownership of the means of production.

questions.stem: A Federal system of government is the one in which
options: power is concentrated in the hands of one of the governments
subordinate units of government exercise sovereign power
the state governors can sue the central government
power is shared between the central government and local governments
power is shared between the central and state governments
questions.explanation: Federalism constitutionally divides power between the central government and the component state governments.

questions.topic: Pressure groups: definition, types, functions and modes of operation
questions.stem: The membership of pressure groups is limited because they
options: are mainly concerned with public interests
questions.explanation: Pressure groups pursue narrow, specific interests, so they attract only people who share those interests.

questions.stem: The OAU was founded to
options: effect an immediate political union of African States
promote the unity and solidarity of African states
create a common market in sub-Saharan Africa
prevent other regional groups from being set up in Africa
questions.explanation: The OAU Charter (1963) aimed chiefly at promoting the unity and solidarity of African states.

questions.stem: Under the present local government system in Nigeria, local councils get the bulk of their finances from
options: fines and penalties by the courts
questions.explanation: After the 1976 reforms, statutory allocations from the Federation Account (federal government) formed the bulk of local council revenue.

questions.stem: The United Nations Organization was founded to
options: co-ordinate the activities of all its members
co-ordinate the activities of regional organizations
questions.explanation: The UN was set up in 1945 primarily to maintain international peace and security.

questions.stem: Before it became effective, the 1979 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria was finally approved by
questions.explanation: After the Constituent Assembly, the Supreme Military Council amended and promulgated the 1979 Constitution by decree in 1978.

questions.stem: Byelaws are usually made and enforced by
questions.explanation: Bye-laws are rules made by local government authorities for their areas.

questions.stem: One of the earliest political institutions set up in the colonial period to allow for local participation in politics was the
questions.explanation: The Legislative Council (from 1862 in Lagos, 1923 elective) was the earliest body admitting Nigerians into colonial politics.

questions.stem: The Organization of African Unity was set up in
questions.explanation: The OAU was founded at Addis Ababa on 25 May 1963.

questions.stem: The Nigeria 1979 Constitution gives the right to vote to
options: all Nigerians below the age of seventeen
all Nigerians of eighteen years and above
questions.explanation: The 1979 Constitution granted universal adult suffrage to citizens aged 18 and above.

questions.stem: The Nigeria 1981 Revenue Allocation Act entitled the local governments to?
questions.explanation: The Allocation of Revenue (Federation Account, etc.) Act 1981 gave local governments 10% of the Federation Account.

questions.topic: The Legislative (post-independence): structures, functions and workings
questions.stem: The Nigeria Federal Legislature is
questions.explanation: The National Assembly has two chambers: the Senate and the House of Representatives.

questions.stem: Ghana was led into independence by
questions.explanation: Kwame Nkrumah and his CPP led the Gold Coast to independence as Ghana in 1957.

questions.stem: Which of the following was the last Constitution formulated for Nigeria without Nigerian participation?
questions.explanation: The Richards Constitution was imposed without consulting Nigerians; the Macpherson Constitution followed wide consultation.

questions.stem: Which of the parties listed below was founded by Herbert Macaulay in 1923?
options: The National Council of Nigerian Citizens
questions.explanation: Herbert Macaulay founded the NNDP in 1923 to contest the Lagos Legislative Council seats.

questions.topic: The Executive (post-independence): structure, functions and workings
questions.stem: In which of the following institutions does the 1979 Constitution of Nigeria provide for the representation of traditional rulers?
questions.explanation: The Council of State under the 1979 Constitution included a representative (chairman of the council of chiefs) from each state.

questions.stem: The Economic Commission for Africa is an agency of
questions.explanation: The ECA is one of the UN's regional economic commissions.

questions.stem: Where is the administrative headquarters of ECOWAS?
questions.explanation: As at 1982 the ECOWAS Executive Secretariat was in Lagos (it later moved to Abuja).

questions.stem: Under the 1979 Nigerian Constitution, State Electoral Commissions are to conduct
options: elections into state Houses of Assembly
questions.explanation: FEDECO conducted federal and state elections, while State Electoral Commissions conducted local government elections.

questions.stem: The Richards Constitution in Nigeria provided for the
options: unofficial majority in the Legislative Council
appointment of Nigerians as Chief Judges
House of Chiefs in the Western Region
House of Chiefs in the Eastern Region
banning of the Trade Union Movement
questions.explanation: The Richards Constitution (1946) gave the Legislative Council an unofficial majority for the first time.

questions.stem: Which of the following countries operates a single party system?
questions.explanation: In 1982 Tanzania was a one-party state under the ruling party (TANU, later CCM).

questions.stem: The main function of the Legislative Council in British Colonial West Africa was to
options: act as a disciplinary body for the civil servants
questions.explanation: Colonial Legislative Councils were largely advisory; the Governor retained final authority.

questions.stem: The judicial organ of the United Nations is the
questions.explanation: The International Court of Justice at The Hague is the principal judicial organ of the UN.

questions.stem: Which of the following countries has the right to veto the decision of the Security Council?
questions.explanation: China is one of the five permanent members with veto power.

questions.stem: The primary function of the Economic and Social Council of the UN is to
options: improve the social relationship between the USA and the Soviet Union
assist in the development of member states
lift customs barriers between petroleum producing and non-petroleum producing countries
encourage trade between Third World and European countries
questions.explanation: ECOSOC co-ordinates the economic and social development work of the UN for member states.

questions.stem: Which of the following countries voted 'no' in the referendum conducted by France in 1958?
questions.explanation: Guinea under Sékou Touré rejected de Gaulle's Community proposal in 1958 and became independent.

questions.stem: Which of the following terms is different from the others?
questions.explanation: Constitutionalism means limited government; the others all denote unlimited, arbitrary rule.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of the parliamentary system of government?
options: Ministers are usually members of parliament
The Prime Minister is politically responsible to the parliament
The Head of State is the most powerful organ of government
The Head of Government may advise the Head of State to dissolve parliament
The party in opposition provides the Shadow Government
questions.explanation: In a parliamentary system the Head of State is ceremonial; real power lies with the Prime Minister and Cabinet.

questions.stem: Capitalism is an economic system in which
options: the economy of the State is centrally planned and controlled
private persons are permitted to undertake enterprises
accumulation of private property is forbidden
the means of production are owned and controlled by the State
all big industries and the land are publicly owned for the common good
questions.explanation: Capitalism rests on private enterprise and private ownership of the means of production.

questions.stem: The process of depriving persons of the right of voting is called
questions.explanation: Disenfranchisement is the removal of the right to vote.

questions.stem: Bicameralism refers to
options: the process of voting in the legislature
the upper chamber in a legislature
questions.explanation: A bicameral legislature has two chambers (houses).

questions.stem: The principle of the separation of powers implies that the three main organs of government work
options: reluctantly and gradually for the executive
together in the interest of other nations
questions.explanation: Each organ is independent in its own sphere but they co-operate (with checks and balances) to run government.

questions.stem: The main function of the judiciary is to
options: serve as the watchdog of the Executive
execute the laws of the land
protect the interest of accused persons
questions.explanation: The judiciary interprets the law and applies it to disputes.

questions.stem: A totalitarian government is
options: a government that aspires to control every aspect of a citizen's life
a government of the people, by the people, and for the people
questions.explanation: Totalitarianism seeks total control over every aspect of public and private life.

questions.stem: An unwritten constitution operates in
questions.explanation: Britain's constitution is not codified in a single document.

questions.stem: A sovereign state is one
options: whose constitution can only be changed by a military government
where its citizens can speak without fear or favour
in which sovereignty is invested in the military
whose citizens are free to evade responsibility
whose government decisions are made independent of foreign interference
questions.explanation: Sovereignty means the state makes its decisions free of external control.

questions.stem: Representative Democracy is best characterized by

questions.stem: An electoral system in which the candidate who receives the largest number of votes wins is
