questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT usually associated with the activities of political parties?
options: selecting and supporting candidates for public office
questions.explanation: Parties do not control the judiciary, which should be independent.

questions.stem: The political neutrality of civil servants is guaranteed by not allowing them to
options: be members of any interest group
questions.explanation: Key printed D; correct answer is C because civil servants may vote and must work with politicians, but are barred from partisan politics to keep them neutral.

questions.stem: An unwritten constitution is one which
options: relies on the memories of elders and priests
codifies the basic laws in one document
embodies the basic laws in more than one document
questions.explanation: An unwritten constitution is not codified in a single document; its rules are found in many statutes, conventions and documents.

questions.stem: Fascism is a system of government which
options: promotes the international brotherhood of man
questions.explanation: Fascism suppresses opposition and dissent.

questions.stem: In a modern democracy the ultimate source of sovereignty is the
questions.explanation: In a democracy political sovereignty ultimately rests with the people.

questions.stem: Which of these is a common feature of totalitarian regimes?
questions.explanation: Totalitarian regimes allow only one recognized party.

questions.stem: Which of the following, according to Marx, is the correct order in which societies progress?
questions.explanation: Marx saw history moving from feudalism to capitalism, then socialism and finally communism.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT necessarily a characteristic of a nation-state?
questions.explanation: A nation-state need not have one common language.

questions.topic: Public opinion: meaning, formation and measurement
questions.stem: Public opinion refers to views and ideas expressed by
options: citizens regarding government policies or other issues
elites about what the public wants
questions.explanation: Public opinion is the views of citizens on public issues and policies.

questions.stem: An issue over which both the centre and the states can exercise authority in a federal system is
questions.explanation: Matters on the concurrent list can be handled by both federal and state governments.

questions.stem: In traditional Hausa-Fulani political system, political authority was vested in the
questions.explanation: The Emir held supreme political and religious authority.

questions.stem: Which of the following pre-independence organizations was formed in London in 1945?
questions.explanation: Egbe Omo Oduduwa was founded in London in 1945 by Awolowo and others.

questions.stem: Igbo traditional system of government encouraged participation through
questions.explanation: The village/town assembly allowed adult males to participate directly.

questions.stem: In the 1950s, the Northern Elements Progressive Union was notable in Nigerian politics because it
options: agitated for the formation of a unitary form of government
allied with the Northern People's Congress to form the regional government
won the election to the Northern House of Assembly
questions.explanation: NEPU, led by Aminu Kano, opposed the autocracy of the Northern emirs.

questions.stem: The author of the famous book Renascent Africa which inspired African nationalism is
questions.explanation: Nnamdi Azikiwe wrote Renascent Africa (1937).

questions.stem: The civil service was first regionalized by the
questions.explanation: The 1954 Lyttleton (federal) Constitution created regional public services.

questions.stem: The motion by Anthony Enahoro demanding independence for Nigeria was moved in
questions.explanation: Enahoro moved the self-government-in-1956 motion in 1953.

questions.stem: The office of the prime minister of Nigeria was first created by the
questions.explanation: The 1957 London conference created the office of Federal Prime Minister, filled by Tafawa Balewa.

questions.stem: Southern Nigeria was divided into Eastern and Western Provinces for administrative purposes in
questions.explanation: Key printed A; correct answer is C because the Southern Provinces were split into Eastern and Western Provinces in 1939.

questions.stem: Which of the following aroused and promoted nationalistic feeling among Nigerians?
options: slave trade, indirect rule and amalgamation
economic exploitation, racial discrimination and political parties
communal riots, news media and religious differences
traditional rulers, district officers and governors-general
questions.explanation: Economic exploitation, racial discrimination and the rise of political parties stirred nationalism.

questions.stem: The leader of the Northern People's Congress was
questions.explanation: Sir Ahmadu Bello, Sardauna of Sokoto, led the NPC.

questions.stem: The Queen of England ceased to be the head of state of Nigeria at
options: the attainment of self-government by the regions
the adoption of the Republican Constitution in October 1963
the inception of the presidential system in October 1979
questions.explanation: Nigeria became a republic on 1 October 1963, replacing the Queen with a president.

questions.stem: The 1963 Constitution of Nigeria was
questions.explanation: The 1963 constitution was written and required special procedures to amend (rigid).

questions.stem: The major political parties in Nigeria during the first Republic were
questions.explanation: The NPC, NCNC and AG were the three major First Republic parties.

questions.stem: The main source of local government finance since the 1976 Reform has been
options: revenue from court fines and licenses
questions.explanation: Statutory allocations from the federal level became the main source of local government revenue.

questions.topic: The Executive (post-independence): structure, functions and workings
questions.stem: Under the 1979 Constitution of Nigeria, the president of the federal republic could only be removed from office by
options: a motion approved by at least two-thirds of all the state houses of assembly
questions.explanation: Impeachment under the 1979 Constitution required action by both houses of the National Assembly.

questions.topic: The Judiciary (post-independence): structure, functions and workings
questions.stem: Under the 1979 Constitution of Nigeria, the head of the judiciary was the
options: Solicitor-General and Permanent Secretary, Federal Ministry of Justice
Chief Registrar of the Supreme Court
questions.explanation: The Chief Justice of the Federation heads the Nigerian judiciary.

questions.topic: Public Commissions Established by the 1979 and Subsequent Constitutions
questions.stem: Ombudsman as an institution in Nigeria is known as the
questions.explanation: Nigeria's ombudsman is the Public Complaints Commission.

questions.stem: Which of the following sets of nations belong to both ECOWAS and the UNO?
questions.explanation: As at 1989 Ghana and Mauritania were both ECOWAS and UN members (Mauritania left ECOWAS in 2000); Uganda, Zimbabwe and Cameroon are not ECOWAS members.

questions.stem: Fundamental human rights of citizens are provided for in
questions.explanation: Chapter IV of the 1979 Constitution guaranteed the fundamental rights of Nigerian citizens.

questions.stem: The head of the Commonwealth of Nations is the
options: chairman of the Conference of the Commonwealth Heads of Governments
questions.explanation: The British monarch is Head of the Commonwealth.

questions.stem: Which of the following principles does NOT govern Nigeria's foreign policy?
questions.explanation: Terrorism is not a principle of any state's foreign policy.

questions.topic: Africa as the “centre piece” of Nigeria’s foreign policy
questions.stem: During the struggle for Angolan independence Nigeria supported
questions.explanation: Nigeria recognised and supported the MPLA in 1975.

questions.stem: Within the United Nations, the veto power is exercised in
questions.explanation: Only the five permanent members of the Security Council hold the veto.

questions.topic: Differences between pressure groups and political parties
questions.stem: Which of the following functions is performed by both political parties and pressure groups?
options: Working for the interest of their members
questions.explanation: Both parties and pressure groups articulate interests and press them on government; only parties contest elections or form the formal opposition.

questions.stem: The exercise of political power involves
questions.explanation: Key printed A; correct answer is D because, following Easton's definition, politics and the exercise of political power are the authoritative allocation of values in society; winning elections is only one way of acquiring power.

questions.stem: Sovereignty is limited by
questions.explanation: A state's sovereignty is externally limited by international law and treaty obligations it accepts.

questions.stem: The pronouncements of judges which have the force of law are called
questions.explanation: Decisions of superior courts that bind later courts are judicial precedents (case law).

questions.stem: Constitutional disputes between states in a federation can only be settled by
questions.explanation: Disputes between component units of a federation are within the original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court.

questions.topic: Electoral System: types, advantages and disadvantages of each
questions.stem: The second ballot is based on the principle that a successful candidate must obtain
questions.explanation: The second (run-off) ballot is held so that the winner obtains an absolute majority (more than half) of the votes.

questions.topic: Election: types and ingredients of a free and fair election
questions.stem: Which of the following is the least democratic selection process?
questions.explanation: Co-option fills a position by invitation of existing members, with no vote by the electorate at all.

questions.stem: An indispensable aspect of the constitution of a democratic state is
questions.explanation: Guaranteed fundamental human rights are essential to a democratic constitution; democracy can be presidential or parliamentary.

questions.stem: A good democratic constitution should aspire to evolve the following EXCEPT
options: a judiciary dependent on the executive
genuine and truly national political parties
a free and fair electoral system
the establishment of the principle of accountability for public officers
questions.explanation: Democracy requires an independent judiciary, not one dependent on the executive.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT characteristic of democracy?
questions.explanation: Democracy rests on universal adult suffrage; a limited franchise is undemocratic.

questions.stem: The principle of separation of powers is fundamental to the
questions.explanation: The presidential system separates the executive from the legislature in personnel and function; the parliamentary system fuses them.

questions.stem: Under socialism, the control of power resides with the
questions.explanation: Socialist theory places control of power and the means of production with the working class (proletariat).

questions.stem: The rule of law implies that
options: everyone is subject to the law
questions.explanation: The rule of law means the supremacy of law, with everyone, rulers included, subject to it.

questions.stem: A by-law is made by
questions.explanation: By-laws are laws made by local government councils for their areas.

questions.stem: The notion of 'carpet-crossing' in a parliamentary democracy involves
options: crossing from the Lower house to the Upper house
questions.explanation: Carpet-crossing is a legislator leaving the party on whose platform he was elected for another party.

questions.stem: In a parliament, the most extensive amendment to a bill takes place at the
questions.explanation: Detailed clause-by-clause scrutiny and amendment of a bill takes place at the committee stage.

questions.topic: Political Processes: Political Socialization, Political Participation, Political Culture
questions.stem: A set of internalized norms which guides political action is called
questions.explanation: Key printed A; correct answer is B because internalized norms and beliefs that guide political behaviour are political values (part of political culture), whereas power is the ability to compel.

questions.stem: Freedom of speech in a democratic state is limited by
questions.explanation: In a democracy free speech is limited by laws such as sedition and defamation; censorship and martial law are undemocratic.

questions.stem: Habeas corpus is an essential process for safeguarding the right of citizens to
questions.explanation: A writ of habeas corpus requires a detained person to be produced in court, protecting personal liberty.

questions.topic: Public opinion: meaning, formation and measurement
questions.stem: The most effective way of monitoring public opinion is
options: by examining the questions asked by journalists
by the frequency of the press releases of pressure groups
questions.explanation: Opinion polls are the standard, systematic way of measuring public opinion on many issues.

questions.stem: In a true democracy, franchise can be limited by
questions.explanation: Key printed D; correct answer is C because universal adult suffrage restricts the vote only by age (and citizenship); restrictions by sex, education or wealth are undemocratic.

questions.stem: Liberalism is a philosophy underlying
questions.explanation: Liberalism, with its emphasis on individual freedom and private enterprise, underlies capitalism.

questions.stem: Which of the following served as the electoral college during the election into the Constituent Assembly in 1978?
questions.explanation: Members of the 1977/78 Constituent Assembly were elected by the newly elected local government councils acting as electoral colleges.

questions.stem: Traditional rulers in Nigeria exercised the greatest political power under
questions.explanation: Under indirect rule the British governed through traditional rulers, who then held their greatest political power.

questions.stem: During the second republic, some local government councils were created by
questions.explanation: In the Second Republic several state governments created new local government councils on their own.

questions.stem: The principal objective of British colonial policy in Nigeria was to
options: lay a solid foundation for Nigerian independence
help build a virile Nigerian economy
exploit and expropriate Nigerian resources for British interests
questions.explanation: Colonial rule was chiefly aimed at exploiting the colony's resources for the benefit of Britain.

questions.stem: Which of the following factors contributed most to cash crop production during the colonial administration in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Key printed C; correct answer is D because colonial taxes payable in cash compelled farmers to grow export cash crops to earn money; forced labour was used mainly for public works.

questions.stem: Under the military regime in Nigeria, state enactments are known as
questions.explanation: Under military rule federal enactments were decrees and state enactments were edicts.

questions.stem: The military normally belongs to the arm(s) of government known as
questions.explanation: The armed forces are part of the executive arm, under the head of the executive as commander-in-chief.

questions.stem: The first political party in Nigeria was the
options: National Council of Nigeria and the Cameroons
questions.explanation: Herbert Macaulay founded the Nigerian National Democratic Party in 1923, Nigeria's first political party.

questions.topic: Problems of Nigerian Federalism and solutions
questions.stem: The major problem of the Nigerian federal structure in the first republic was
options: lopsided size of the component units
questions.explanation: Key printed A; correct answer is C because the question is about the federal structure, whose main defect was that the Northern Region was larger than all the other regions combined, enabling it to dominate the federation.

questions.stem: The legislative organ of the Federal Government in the first republic was the
questions.explanation: Key printed D; correct answer is A because the First Republic's federal legislature was the Parliament (House of Representatives and Senate); the National Assembly was the Second Republic's legislature.

questions.stem: Which of the following was the LEAST important rationale for Nigerian federalism?
options: The vastness of the territory and the size of the population
questions.explanation: A bicameral legislature is a feature that federalism often adopts, not a reason for choosing federalism.

questions.stem: One of the agreements of the 1957 constitutional conference was that
options: Southern Cameroons should constitute a separate region
a House of Chiefs was to be created in the Western Region
the office of the speaker of the House of Representatives was to be created
the police was to be regionalized
questions.explanation: The 1957 London conference agreed that Southern Cameroons should become a full region with its own premier; the Western House of Chiefs already existed and the police was not regionalized.

questions.stem: The two nationalist leaders who led the tour of Northern Nigeria in 1946 to campaign against the Richards Constitution were
options: Ahmadu Bello and Abubakar Tafawa Balewa
Ahmadu Bello and Samuel Ladoke Akintola
questions.explanation: The NCNC's 1946 nationwide tour against the Richards Constitution was led by Macaulay (who died in Kano during it) and Azikiwe.

questions.stem: The motion of self-government was moved in 1953 by the
options: National Council of Nigeria and the Cameroons
questions.explanation: Anthony Enahoro of the Action Group moved the 1953 motion for self-government in 1956.

questions.stem: Which of the following had a centralized administration in pre-colonial Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The Yoruba (Oyo) had a centralized monarchical system; the Igbo, Tiv and Ibibio were acephalous.

questions.stem: In which of the following states was the governor impeached during the second republic?
questions.explanation: Governor Balarabe Musa of Kaduna State was impeached by the state assembly in 1981.

questions.stem: The Economic Commission for Africa is an agency of
questions.explanation: The ECA is one of the regional commissions of the United Nations.

questions.stem: Which of the following pairs of countries were trust territories of the United Nations?
questions.explanation: Togo was a UN trust territory and Namibia (South West Africa) was a former mandate placed under UN responsibility; Ghana, Niger, Botswana and Zaire were not.

questions.stem: The headquarters of the O.A.U. Liberation Committee is located in
questions.explanation: The OAU Liberation (Coordinating) Committee was based in Dar-es-Salaam, Tanzania.

questions.stem: Which of the following groups advocated for political union of African States?
questions.explanation: The radical Casablanca Group (Nkrumah and others) wanted immediate political union; the Monrovia Group favoured gradual cooperation.

questions.stem: Nigeria's first external affairs minister was
questions.explanation: Jaja Wachuku became Nigeria's first Minister of External (Foreign) Affairs in 1961.

questions.stem: The first conference of the Non-Aligned Movement was held in
questions.explanation: The first Non-Aligned summit was held in Belgrade in 1961; Bandung (1955) was its Afro-Asian forerunner.

questions.stem: Which of these countries is NOT a member of the Commonwealth of Nations?
questions.explanation: As at 1990 Rwanda, a former Belgian territory, was not a Commonwealth member (it joined only in 2009).

questions.stem: In international relations, countries have a right to
questions.explanation: International law (the Vienna Convention) gives states the right to diplomatic immunity for their envoys.

questions.stem: An indispensable feature of any government is
questions.explanation: Every government, whatever its form, must possess political power to make and enforce decisions; the other features are found only in some systems.

questions.stem: The unrestrained power of a state over its citizens defines the concept of
questions.explanation: Sovereignty is the supreme, unrestrained power of the state over all persons within its territory.

questions.stem: Case-laws are made by the
questions.explanation: Case law (judge-made law) arises from the decisions of the courts.

questions.stem: Which of the following undermines the independence of the judiciary?
options: the confirmation of the appointment of the chief justice by the legislature
payment of the salaries of judicial officers by government
making the minister of justice the attorney-general
questions.explanation: Widespread use of special tribunals takes cases away from the regular courts and weakens judicial independence; legislative confirmation of appointments and paying salaries from public funds are normal safeguards.

questions.stem: Bicameral legislatures are popular in
questions.explanation: Federations commonly use a second chamber to give equal representation to the component units.

questions.stem: One of the weaknesses of confederation is the
questions.explanation: Because the component states retain sovereignty, a confederation is weak at the centre and prone to members seceding.

questions.stem: A system of government which emphasizes co-ordinate status of component units is referred to as
questions.explanation: Key printed A; correct answer is B because K.C. Wheare defines federalism as a system in which the central and regional governments are co-ordinate and independent within their spheres; in a unitary system the units are subordinate.

questions.stem: A flexible constitution is one that is
questions.explanation: A flexible constitution can be amended by the ordinary law-making process.

questions.stem: Unlike the British, the United States constitution is
questions.explanation: The US constitution is written, rigid and federal; the British constitution is unwritten, flexible and unitary.

questions.stem: The terms oligarchy and democracy identify governments according to
options: the number of people who participate in it
formal distribution of power among governmental levels
questions.explanation: Aristotle's classification by number of rulers: rule by a few (oligarchy) or by the many (democracy).

questions.stem: Governments whose central concern is the equitable distribution of wealth are said to be
questions.explanation: Socialism aims at equitable distribution of wealth through collective ownership.

questions.stem: The presidential system of government ensures
options: democratic rule more than other systems
the sharing of executive power with the legislature
the concentration of power in the chief executive
questions.explanation: In the presidential system all executive power is concentrated in the president as head of state and government.

questions.topic: Relationships among the arms of government
questions.stem: The notion of checks and balances guarantees that
options: the executive is able to control the legislature
the judiciary can stop all executive actions
each branch of government acts as a watchdog over other branches
the legislature is subordinate to the judiciary
questions.explanation: Checks and balances let each arm of government restrain the others so none abuses power.

questions.stem: The principle of collective responsibility implies that
options: the prime minister can dissolve the entire parliament
the head of state can dismiss the prime minister
each offending minister can be reassigned
the cabinet stands or falls together
questions.explanation: Collective responsibility means all ministers share responsibility for cabinet decisions and stand or fall together.

questions.stem: The application of the rule of law may be constrained by
options: securing the tenure of office of judges
employing men of proven integrity as judges
questions.explanation: Emergency powers allow suspension of normal rights and procedures, limiting the rule of law; the other options strengthen it.

questions.stem: A device for controlling prolonged debates in parliament is called
questions.explanation: The guillotine is a time-allocation motion that cuts off debate at set times.

questions.stem: In the parliamentary system, when parliament defeats a major government bill, the
options: opposition immediately forms a new government
questions.explanation: Defeat on a major bill is treated as loss of confidence, and under collective responsibility the cabinet resigns.

questions.stem: A bill becomes an Act of Parliament after it has been
options: signed by the head of state
processed through the committee of the house
questions.explanation: A bill passed by parliament becomes law only on receiving the assent of the head of state.

questions.stem: The primary duty of citizens to the state is
questions.explanation: The first duty of a citizen is loyalty and allegiance to the state and its lawful government.

questions.stem: Individual rights are said to be inalienable if they
options: apply to citizens and aliens alike
cannot be denied under any circumstances
can only be denied by the legislature
can only be denied after due legal process
questions.explanation: Key printed C; correct answer is B because 'inalienable' means the rights cannot be taken away or surrendered under any circumstances.

questions.topic: Election: types and ingredients of a free and fair election
questions.stem: Elections present the electorate the opportunity to
options: assess the performances of the previous representatives
questions.explanation: The basic purpose of an election is to let voters choose among competing candidates.

questions.topic: Election: types and ingredients of a free and fair election
questions.stem: The process of removing an elected official by the electorate after an election is termed
questions.explanation: Recall lets the electorate remove its representative before the end of the term; impeachment is by the legislature.

questions.topic: Pressure groups: definition, types, functions and modes of operation
questions.stem: Groups which seek to bring about changes in government policies without actually controlling the personnel of government are known as
questions.explanation: Pressure groups seek to influence policy but do not seek to capture government.

questions.stem: Which of the following traditional political systems was segmentary?
questions.explanation: The pre-colonial Igbo political system was segmentary (acephalous), without a central authority.

questions.stem: Which of the following led to the introduction of indirect rule in Nigeria by the British?
questions.explanation: Lugard adopted indirect rule chiefly because there were too few British officials to administer the vast territory directly.

questions.stem: Warrant Chiefs were appointed to
questions.explanation: Warrant chiefs were appointed in Eastern Nigeria to run local administration under indirect rule where no traditional chiefs existed.

questions.stem: The 1946 Constitution is characterized by
options: official majority in the legislative council
non-official majority in the legislative council
non-official majority in the executive council
questions.explanation: The Richards Constitution of 1946 introduced an unofficial majority in the Legislative Council.

questions.stem: The Willink Commission was set up to
options: examine issues relating to the welfare of groups
questions.explanation: The 1957 Willink Commission inquired into the fears of minorities and the means of allaying them.

questions.stem: The state legislatures of the second republic in Nigeria had the following EXCEPT
questions.explanation: State Houses of Assembly were unicameral, with a speaker, deputy speaker and clerk; there was no senate at state level.

questions.topic: Tiers of government and their relationship
questions.stem: Which of these constitutions recognised local government as the third tier of government?
questions.explanation: The 1979 Constitution, following the 1976 reforms, recognised local government as the third tier.

questions.topic: The Judiciary (post-independence): structure, functions and workings
questions.stem: A condition for judicial independence is the appointment of judges by the
questions.explanation: Appointment on the advice of an independent Judicial Service Commission insulates judges from political control.

questions.stem: The federal system of government in Nigeria was abolished in favour of a unitary one by
questions.explanation: Ironsi's Unification Decree No. 34 of May 1966 abolished the federation.

questions.stem: One of the measures taken in 1988 to grant more autonomy to the local governments in Nigeria was the
options: abolition of state ministries of local government
creation of post of supervisory councillors
creation of post of chairmen of local governments
abolition of its supervision by state government
questions.explanation: In 1988 the Babangida government abolished state ministries of local government to free councils from state control.

questions.stem: Traditional rulers were restricted to ceremonial roles by the Local Government Reforms of
questions.explanation: The 1976 reforms removed executive powers from traditional rulers and gave them advisory/ceremonial roles.

questions.topic: Election: types and ingredients of a free and fair election
questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT associated with local government elections?
questions.explanation: Local government councillors are elected from wards; constituencies are used for legislative elections.

questions.stem: The Public Service Review Commission of 1991 made proposals to ensure that the public service was
options: more effective than the private sector
more attractive than the private sector
questions.explanation: The civil service reforms of the period aimed at an efficient, result-oriented public service.

questions.stem: Under military regime, the branches of government that become fused are the
options: judiciary, the executive and the legislature
questions.explanation: Military rulers combine legislative and executive powers in the ruling council while the courts continue to operate.

questions.stem: Nigeria is NOT a member of the
options: Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development
questions.explanation: The OECD is an organisation of industrialised countries; Nigeria belongs to the NAM, OPEC and the IMF.

questions.stem: Nigeria broke diplomatic relations with France under the Balewa government over
questions.explanation: Balewa's government broke relations with France in 1961 over French atomic tests in the Sahara.

questions.stem: The Obasanjo administration nationalized the assets of British Petroleum over the British government's policy in
questions.explanation: In 1979 Nigeria nationalised BP's assets to pressure Britain over Rhodesia (Zimbabwe).

questions.stem: Nigerian foreign policy implementation is the responsibility of the
questions.explanation: The Ministry of External (Foreign) Affairs executes Nigeria's foreign policy.

questions.stem: The head of a Nigerian mission in a Commonwealth country is called
questions.explanation: Commonwealth countries exchange High Commissioners rather than ambassadors.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a statutory function of an embassy?
questions.explanation: Espionage is not a lawful diplomatic function under international law.

questions.stem: ECOWAS is aimed at uniting the West African states
questions.explanation: ECOWAS was established in 1975 primarily to promote economic integration.

questions.stem: Which of the following countries pioneered the idea of ECOWAS alongside Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Nigeria's Gowon and Togo's Eyadema championed the formation of ECOWAS.

questions.stem: Which of these countries was NOT a foundation member of the Organization of African Unity?
questions.explanation: Zimbabwe became independent only in 1980, long after the OAU was founded in 1963.

questions.stem: The United Nations was founded with the primary objective of
options: uniting all nations into a world federation
questions.explanation: The UN's primary purpose is the maintenance of international peace and security.

questions.stem: Until her independence, Namibia was a
questions.explanation: Namibia (South West Africa) was a former League mandate for which the UN assumed direct responsibility; it was never formally a South African province and ceased to be German in 1915.

questions.stem: A political authority which exercises sovereign power over a specific geographical area is termed a
questions.explanation: A state is a people in a defined territory under a government exercising sovereign power.

questions.topic: Political Processes: Political Socialization, Political Participation, Political Culture
questions.stem: The process by which political beliefs and values are transmitted from one generation to another is best known as political
questions.explanation: Political socialization is the transmission of political values and beliefs across generations.

questions.stem: The fusion of the executive and legislative organs of government is associated with
questions.explanation: In the parliamentary system ministers are members of the legislature, fusing the two organs.

questions.stem: One criticism of delegated legislation is that it
options: is not useful in emergency situations
questions.explanation: Key printed D; correct answer is A because the standard criticism of delegated legislation is that it lets the executive and its agencies make binding rules for citizens without full parliamentary scrutiny; usefulness in emergencies is an advantage, and the printed option D is not a valid criticism.

questions.stem: A system of government in which the central government is supreme over other levels is
questions.explanation: Key printed C; correct answer is D because in a unitary system all power belongs to the central government and lower levels exist at its pleasure, whereas in a federation the levels are co-ordinate.

questions.stem: Which of the following defines a constitution?
options: Basic laws for the conduct of modern government
The doctrine that limits the power of government
questions.explanation: A constitution is the body of fundamental laws and rules by which a state is governed.

questions.stem: Which of the following ideologies advocates governmental control over all sources of power?
questions.explanation: Totalitarianism seeks total state control of all aspects of social, economic and political life.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT an acceptable means of achieving democracy?
questions.explanation: Referendum, recall and initiative are lawful instruments of direct democracy; riots are not.

questions.stem: The principle of collective responsibility does not operate under the presidential system of government because
options: the legislative and the executive work together
the executive is elected for a fixed term
the judiciary will overrule the impeachment of the cabinet
questions.explanation: The president is elected for a fixed term and is not removable by a vote of no confidence, so the cabinet does not stand or fall together before the legislature.

questions.stem: Law making under military regimes is done through
questions.explanation: Military governments legislate by promulgating decrees (and edicts at state level).

questions.stem: The most critical debates on a bill and amendments to it take place during the
questions.explanation: Key printed C; correct answer is B because the second reading is where the principles of the bill are fully debated (followed by the committee stage for amendments); the third reading is usually a brief formal stage.

questions.stem: The fundamental rights of citizens include
options: immunity from libel and right to employment
questions.explanation: Key printed C; correct answer is D because the right to life and the right to personal liberty are core fundamental rights, while immunity from libel and a right to employment are not.

questions.topic: Electoral System: types, advantages and disadvantages of each
questions.stem: Electoral colleges have been criticized because they
options: create more seats in the legislature
sometimes negate the wishes of the electorate
questions.explanation: Indirect election through colleges can produce results different from the voters' choice.

questions.stem: Universal adult suffrage is usually restricted in most political systems to
options: those not more than 70 years old
questions.explanation: Universal adult suffrage is normally confined to adult citizens of the state.

questions.topic: Election: types and ingredients of a free and fair election
questions.stem: An election in which citizens are called upon to vote for or against a specified issue is called a
questions.explanation: A referendum submits a specific issue directly to the electorate.

questions.stem: The most important objective of political parties is to
questions.explanation: Political parties aim primarily to win power and control the government.

questions.topic: Pressure groups: definition, types, functions and modes of operation
questions.stem: The primary function of a pressure group is to
questions.explanation: Pressure groups seek to influence public policy without seeking to form the government.

questions.topic: Public opinion: meaning, formation and measurement
questions.stem: The biased presentation of information in order to influence public opinion is referred to as
questions.explanation: Propaganda is the deliberate, one-sided presentation of information to shape opinion.

questions.stem: Which of the following was a great military and political power before the colonization of Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The Kwararafa (Jukun) empire was a major military power that raided Hausa states and Borno.

questions.stem: The Yoruba traditional governmental system was
questions.explanation: The Yoruba (Oyo) system was a monarchy headed by the Oba/Alaafin, checked by councils such as the Oyomesi.

questions.stem: During the pre-colonial period in Eastern Nigeria autocratic rule was made difficult by the
options: absence of a system of centralized authority
questions.explanation: The Igbo were acephalous, with power dispersed among elders, age grades and assemblies, so no autocrat could emerge.

questions.stem: Vassalage as a political system was practised by the
questions.explanation: The Hausa-Fulani emirates were vassal states owing allegiance and tribute to Sokoto or Gwandu.

questions.stem: Which of the following was NOT a feature of colonial administration in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Forced labour, low produce prices and taxation were features of colonial rule; an education levy was not.

questions.stem: Dual mandate was proposed by
questions.explanation: Lugard set out the dual mandate in 'The Dual Mandate in British Tropical Africa' (1922).

questions.stem: The Northern People's Congress stand during the nationalist struggle for Nigeria's independence was
questions.explanation: The NPC opposed the 1953 self-government-in-1956 motion and favoured independence 'as soon as practicable'.

questions.stem: The Aba women riot was caused by the attempt to introduce
questions.explanation: Key printed C; correct answer is B because the 1929 Aba women's riot was triggered by the rumour that women would be counted for direct taxation; warrant chiefs had existed since about 1900.

questions.stem: One of the unique innovations of the 1951 constitution was the introduction of
options: the office of the prime minister
questions.explanation: The Macpherson Constitution introduced executive councils in the regions; premiers came in 1954 and the prime minister in 1957.

questions.stem: The Constituent Assembly of 1978 had the primary responsibility of
options: drafting a constitution for the Second Republic
deliberating on, debating and amending the draft constitution
conducting a referendum on the draft constitution
questions.explanation: The Constituent Assembly debated and amended the draft prepared by the Constitution Drafting Committee; the military enacted it.

questions.stem: To qualify to be president of the Federal Republic of Nigeria under the 1979 constitution, a candidate must
options: be at least 40 years of age
have the highest number of votes cast at the election
have not less than 1/4 of the votes cast at the election in each of at least 2/3 of all states in the federation
questions.explanation: Section 126 of the 1979 Constitution required a candidate to be a citizen of Nigeria by birth (and at least 35); the vote thresholds relate to winning the election, not qualifying as a candidate.

questions.stem: By statute, the main responsibility of the armed forces of Nigeria is to
options: defend the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the country
take part in peace-keeping operations in troubled neighbouring countries
questions.explanation: The armed forces exist to defend Nigeria from external aggression and maintain its territorial integrity.

questions.topic: The Judiciary (post-independence): structure, functions and workings
questions.stem: The highest court in Nigeria before 1963 was the
options: Judicial Committee of the Privy Council
questions.explanation: Until the 1963 Republican Constitution, final appeals went to the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council in London.

questions.stem: The highest decision-making body in Nigeria under the Buhari regime was the
questions.explanation: Under Buhari (1984-85) the Supreme Military Council was the highest organ; Babangida renamed it the AFRC.

questions.stem: The primary factor which led to the formation of political parties in colonial Nigeria was
options: introduction of the elective principle and representative institutions
increased wealth of the indigenous elite
granting of self government by the colonial administration
call by black people all over the world for a final assault on colonialism
questions.explanation: The elective principle of the 1922 Clifford Constitution led Macaulay to form the NNDP in 1923 to contest elections.

questions.topic: Problems of Nigerian Federalism and solutions
questions.stem: The results of the 1973 census in Nigeria were rejected because
options: the figures were unacceptable to the U.N.
Nigerians were contented with the existing population figures
there were preparations for a fresh census
questions.explanation: The 1973 census figures were disputed as inflated and were cancelled by the Murtala regime in 1975.

questions.stem: One of the advantages of privatization is that it
options: relieves government of its liquidity problem
makes the poor to be richer
gives private individuals control over public corporations
questions.explanation: Privatization is expected to make enterprises more efficient through private management and profit motive.

questions.stem: The most important aspect of the 1976 Local Government Reforms was the
options: introduction of a uniform system of local government
introduction of party politics at the local levels
subordination of local governments to the federal and state governments
recognition of local government as autonomous and sovereign government
questions.explanation: The 1976 reforms established a uniform, single-tier local government system across Nigeria.

questions.stem: Local governments were created in Nigeria mainly to
options: realise the objective of full employment
bring government nearer to the people
prevent the creation of more states
encourage competition and rivalry amongst ethnic groups
questions.explanation: Local government exists mainly to bring government closer to the grassroots.

questions.stem: The Nigerian Military Government launched the Second National Development Plan in 1970 purposely
options: to develop all the disadvantaged states
to accelerate the development of the country
for rapid economic and social development of the country after the civil war
to further the cause of a united, strong and self-reliant nation
questions.explanation: The 1970-74 plan was launched for reconstruction and rapid development after the civil war.

questions.stem: A feature unique to General Murtala Muhammed's Supreme Military Council as compared to that of General Yakubu Gowon was the
options: exclusion of military governors from the council
inclusion of the chief justice as a member
exclusion of the Inspector General of Police from the council
questions.explanation: Murtala removed state military governors from the SMC; under Gowon they were members.

questions.stem: A major problem of military governments in Nigeria is the
options: abolition of the post of ombudsman
absence of the rule of law
questions.explanation: Military rule by decree, ouster clauses and detention without trial undermine the rule of law.

questions.stem: In 1973, following an OAU resolution, Nigeria broke diplomatic relations with
questions.explanation: After the 1973 Arab-Israeli war, African states including Nigeria broke relations with Israel in line with the OAU resolution.

questions.stem: Nigeria's foreign policy of non-alignment was a reaction to
questions.explanation: Non-alignment meant not taking sides in the Cold War rivalry between East and West.

questions.stem: Which of the following countries had a strained relationship with Nigeria over the Angolan crisis of 1975?
questions.explanation: Nigeria recognised the MPLA in 1975 against US pressure, straining relations with the USA.

questions.topic: Africa as the “centre piece” of Nigeria’s foreign policy
questions.stem: The major liberation organization which fought for Namibia's independence was
questions.explanation: Key printed B; correct answer is A because the South West Africa People's Organisation (SWAPO) led Namibia's liberation struggle; the ANC was South African, FRELIMO Mozambican and the MPLA Angolan.

questions.stem: In the first republic, Nigeria was very reluctant to have meaningful interaction with
questions.explanation: The pro-Western Balewa government kept the Soviet Union at arm's length, delaying an embassy until 1961.

questions.stem: Which of these international organizations was the predecessor of the United Nations?
questions.explanation: The League of Nations (1919-46) preceded the UN.

questions.stem: The dramatic rise in the membership of the UN during late 1991 and early 1992 is best accounted for by the
options: admission of a large number of newly independent African states
appointment of the first African as Secretary-General
break-up of the Soviet Union into independent republics
expansion of the membership of the Security Council
questions.explanation: The break-up of the USSR (and Yugoslavia) produced many new states admitted to the UN in 1991-92.

questions.stem: Political authority refers to the
options: capacity to produce desired political results
capacity to reshape the political behaviour of citizens
recognized right to exercise political power
questions.explanation: Authority is power that is recognised as legitimate - the accepted right to exercise power. (Not in the answer-key copy; answered from the definition.)

questions.stem: The sovereignty of a state is determined by
questions.explanation: Key printed D; correct answer is C because sovereignty is analysed as legal sovereignty (the supreme law-making body) and political sovereignty (the electorate/people); economic factors are not its determinants.

questions.stem: The civil service belongs to the organ of government called the
questions.explanation: The civil service is the administrative machinery of the executive arm.

questions.stem: Ultimate power in a confederal state is
options: constitutionally divided between the centre and the units
questions.explanation: In a confederation the member states retain sovereignty; the centre has only delegated powers.

questions.stem: Federalism is a constitutional arrangement in which
options: the national and regional governments derive their power from the constitution
the national government acts only through the regional governments
regional and local authorities exist at the pleasure of national government
the national government does not reach individual citizens directly
questions.explanation: In a federation both levels of government derive their powers directly from the constitution.

questions.stem: A written constitution is one that
options: can only be amended by the highest legislative body
is contained in a single document
questions.explanation: A written constitution is one whose provisions are contained in a single document or a few documents.

questions.stem: A federal system of government can exist without
questions.explanation: Federations may be presidential or parliamentary (e.g. Canada, Australia); division of powers and a supreme constitution are essential.

questions.stem: As a political ideology, communism seeks to
options: concentrate national wealth in the hands of a few
provide adequate opportunities for citizens to make profits
eliminate all forms of socio-economic inequality
questions.explanation: Key printed B; correct answer is D because communism seeks a classless society without socio-economic inequality, based on collective (not private) ownership; option B states the opposite of communism.

questions.topic: Relationships among the arms of government
questions.stem: Despite the doctrine of separation of powers, the legislature plays a quasi-judicial role as a result of its
questions.explanation: Legislative investigations and impeachment proceedings are quasi-judicial in nature.

questions.stem: Nazism as a doctrine was proposed by
questions.explanation: Nazism (National Socialism) was Hitler's doctrine; Mussolini founded fascism.

questions.stem: In the Westminster system of government formal legislation can take the following forms EXCEPT
questions.explanation: Acts of Parliament, Orders in Council and royal proclamations have legal force; a minister's pronouncement does not.

questions.stem: In the presidential system of government, the president is
options: elected only through the electoral college
head of state and head of government
questions.explanation: The executive president combines the roles of head of state and head of government.

questions.stem: Delegated legislation is disadvantageous because it
options: erodes the principle of separation of powers
makes hasty review of legislation possible
increases the work of the legislature
questions.explanation: Delegated legislation lets the executive make law, eroding the separation of powers.

questions.stem: The principle of the rule of law stipulates that
options: law makers are above the law
everyone is equal before the law
questions.explanation: Equality before the law is a core element of Dicey's rule of law.

questions.topic: Electoral System: types, advantages and disadvantages of each
questions.stem: Gerrymandering means
questions.explanation: Gerrymandering is drawing constituency boundaries to favour a party.

questions.topic: Electoral System: types, advantages and disadvantages of each
questions.stem: Another term for an electoral district is a
questions.explanation: An electoral district from which a representative is elected is a constituency.

questions.stem: Franchise ensures
questions.explanation: Key printed D; correct answer is A because the franchise (right to vote) is the means by which citizens participate in public affairs; it does not by itself guarantee equal representation, which depends on the electoral system.

questions.topic: Election: types and ingredients of a free and fair election
questions.stem: Free and fair elections do NOT accommodate
options: obedience to the rules of the game
questions.explanation: A free and fair election requires an impartial electoral body.

questions.topic: Electoral System: types, advantages and disadvantages of each
questions.stem: Proportional representation is often criticized because it
options: tends to preserve the multi-party system
ensures that each party has a minister
provides that each state is represented according to its population
questions.explanation: PR encourages many small parties, which can lead to unstable coalition governments.

questions.topic: Pressure groups: definition, types, functions and modes of operation
questions.stem: Interest groups are important to democracies because they
options: represent groups who otherwise would be left out
provide a forum for confronting the government
questions.explanation: Interest groups give voice to sections of society whose interests might otherwise be ignored.

questions.stem: In the Habe political system the Sarki was assisted in performing his executive functions by the
questions.explanation: In the Habe (Hausa) states the Galadima was a senior official who assisted the Sarki in administration; the alkali and khadi were judges.

questions.stem: In the Oyo empire, the Alaafin was
questions.explanation: The Alaafin's power was checked by the Oyomesi and Ogboni, making him a constitutional monarch.

questions.stem: Which of these sets represents the disadvantages of colonialism?
options: exposure to western education, cultural imperialism and external trade relations
cultural imperialism, external manipulations and foreign control of domestic economy
external manipulation, civil service evolution and liberal democracy
liberal democracy, foreign domination and cultural imperialism
questions.explanation: Each item in B is a negative effect; the other sets mix in benefits such as education or democracy.

questions.stem: Imperialism was adopted by Europe to
options: expand its economic and political base
develop the economies of the colonies
establish a democratic society similar to that of Europe
end ethnic rivalries in the colonies
questions.explanation: European imperialism sought raw materials, markets and political power.

questions.stem: The Lagos Colony and the Southern Protectorate of Nigeria were joined in the year
questions.explanation: The Colony of Lagos was merged with the Protectorate of Southern Nigeria in 1906.

questions.stem: Taubman Goldie was famous for the
options: merger of British companies into the United Africa Company
treaty of friendship and the race to Nikki
questions.explanation: George Taubman Goldie amalgamated rival British firms into the United African Company in 1879, later the Royal Niger Company.

questions.stem: Which of the following internal factors did NOT affect the development of nationalist movements in colonial Nigeria?
options: Denial of equal opportunities to Nigerians vis-a-vis their European counterparts
the establishment of political parties and newspapers
the influx of West Indian and American intellectuals
questions.explanation: The influence of West Indian and American intellectuals was an external, not internal, factor.

questions.stem: One significant aspect of the legislative council of 1922 was that
options: it made laws only for the southern provinces
the colony of Lagos and the protectorate of southern Nigeria were merged
laws governing land ownership in the north were extended to the south
questions.explanation: The 1922 Legislative Council legislated for Lagos and the Southern Provinces; the North was governed by proclamation of the Governor.

questions.stem: The 1960 independence Constitution could be described as written,
questions.explanation: Under the 1960 constitution the British monarch remained head of state (via the Governor-General) within a parliamentary system.

questions.stem: The governor-general of Nigeria at the time of political independence was
questions.explanation: Sir James Robertson was Governor-General at independence in 1960.

questions.stem: Before the collapse of Nigeria's First Republic in 1966, the prime minister was both
options: the head of government and a law maker
the head of state and commander-in-chief of the armed forces
commander-in-chief of the armed forces and party leader
head of state and party leader
questions.explanation: Balewa was head of government and a member of parliament; the President (Azikiwe) was head of state.

questions.topic: Public Commissions Established by the 1979 and Subsequent Constitutions
questions.stem: In Nigeria, the function of the Council of State is
questions.explanation: Key printed C; correct answer is D because the Council of State, established under the 1979 Constitution, advises the President on matters such as the prerogative of mercy, census and appointments; it does not make laws.

questions.topic: Problems of Nigerian Federalism and solutions
questions.stem: Which of the following was an ad hoc Revenue Allocation Commission?
questions.explanation: Key printed C; correct answer is D because the Phillipson Commission (1946) was a revenue allocation commission; the Udoji Commission (1974) reviewed the public service and the Ashby Commission dealt with higher education.

questions.topic: Public corporations: definition, types, purpose and functions
questions.stem: In Nigeria, public corporations are also known as
questions.explanation: Public corporations are commonly called parastatals in Nigeria.

questions.stem: The local government is an example of
questions.explanation: Local government in a federation involves the devolution of power to a lower tier with its own authority.

questions.stem: Diarchy refers to the
options: rule by the government and the opposition parties
mixture of parliamentary and presidential systems
rule by the military and civilians
questions.explanation: Diarchy, as proposed by Azikiwe, means joint rule by the military and civilians.

questions.stem: Nigeria's relations with other nations are determined by her
questions.explanation: National interest is the basis of any country's foreign policy.

questions.topic: Africa as the “centre piece” of Nigeria’s foreign policy
questions.stem: The foreign policy of Nigeria is centred on Africa because of her
options: concern for and attention to African problems
commitment to end colonization in Africa
questions.explanation: Nigeria made Africa the centrepiece of its foreign policy out of concern for African problems generally.

questions.stem: The major organization through which Nigeria pursues her economic, political and social interests in West Africa is
questions.explanation: ECOWAS is the sub-regional organisation for West Africa.

questions.stem: A state is admitted into the United Nations on the
options: recommendation of the secretary general to the security council
concurrent vote of the security council and the general assembly
enabling action of the general assembly
sponsorship of any member of the organization
questions.explanation: Key printed A; correct answer is B because under Article 4 of the UN Charter admission is by decision of the General Assembly on the recommendation of the Security Council; the Secretary-General plays no deciding role.

questions.stem: The highest policy making body of the OAU is the
options: Assembly of Heads of State and Government
questions.explanation: The Assembly of Heads of State and Government was the supreme organ of the OAU.

questions.stem: To which of these bodies did Nigeria belong before the formation of the OAU in 1963?
questions.explanation: Nigeria belonged to the moderate Monrovia Group.

questions.stem: Who was the first Nigerian to be appointed President of the International Court of Justice at the Hague?
questions.explanation: Taslim Olawale Elias became President of the ICJ in 1982.

questions.stem: An agency of the United Nations which specializes in the welfare of children is the
questions.explanation: UNICEF is the UN Children's Fund.

questions.stem: Financial contributions to the liberation movements in Southern Africa by African governments were channelled through the
questions.explanation: African support for liberation movements went through the OAU Liberation Committee.

questions.stem: Prior to 1991, veto power was exercised in the United Nations Security Council by
options: France, Germany, the Soviet Union, Italy and Japan
Japan, the United States, Italy, Germany and France
the Soviet Union, People's Republic of China, Great Britain, France and the United States
Italy, the United States, the Soviet Union, Germany and France
questions.explanation: The five permanent members with veto power were the USSR, China, Britain, France and the USA.

questions.stem: Political power is naked force when it is exercised without
questions.explanation: Key printed D; correct answer is C because power exercised without legitimacy (rightful acceptance) is mere naked force.

questions.stem: The major difference between a state and a nation is that the latter presupposes a
questions.explanation: A nation is a group of people sharing common culture, language and history, i.e. a homogenous population.

questions.stem: The principle of judicial independence makes sense only when judges
options: have freedom to try any case
can join any political party of their choice
questions.explanation: Key printed A; correct answer is C because security of tenure protects judges from removal for unpopular judgements, which is the basis of judicial independence.

questions.stem: A federal system of government has the following three advantages
options: economies of scale, uniform development and political unity
economies of scale, uniform development and strong army
strong army, greater security and economies of scale
economic co-operation, uniform development and greater security
questions.explanation: Federation pools resources (economies of scale), spreads development and holds diverse groups in political unity.

questions.stem: Constitutionalism means
options: electoral processes based on the constitution
questions.explanation: Key printed C; correct answer is B because constitutionalism is the respect for and adherence to the constitution by rulers and ruled.

questions.stem: What is the major distinguishing characteristic between flexible and rigid constitutions?
questions.explanation: A flexible constitution is amended like an ordinary law; a rigid one needs a special amendment procedure.

questions.stem: Which of the following best defines democracy?
options: Government based on virtuous principles and laws
Government based on the spirit and letter of the constitution
Government based on the free consent of the governed
Government which recognizes and respects human rights as enshrined in the constitution
questions.explanation: Democracy is government by the free consent of the governed.

questions.stem: An economic system in which the major means of production are owned and controlled by a few individuals is called
questions.explanation: Under capitalism the means of production are privately owned.

questions.topic: Relationships among the arms of government
questions.stem: The essence of checks and balances is to
options: enhance the functioning of government and prevent arbitrary use of power
ensure that people have their own rights
make sure that power is not delegated to other bodies or individuals
prevent political parties from putting pressure on government
questions.explanation: Each arm checks the others so that none uses power arbitrarily.

questions.stem: The power of a head of state to dissolve the legislature and order a general election is usually associated with the
questions.explanation: In the parliamentary system the head of state, on the advice of the prime minister, dissolves parliament.

questions.stem: Accountability in public office means that officers shall
options: keep proper account of state finances
render good account of their activities
questions.explanation: Accountability means public officers answer for (render account of) their actions.

questions.stem: The act of bringing a legislative session to an end only for business to continue later is called
questions.explanation: Key printed A; correct answer is B because prorogation ends a session of the legislature without dissolving it, so business resumes in the next session; adjournment only suspends a sitting.

questions.stem: Which of the following violates the principle of the rule of law?
options: Arbitrary increases of prices by traders
Criticism of government actions by the press
Arbitrariness of individuals in the society
questions.explanation: The rule of law forbids arbitrary use of power by government.

questions.topic: Duties and obligations of the state
questions.stem: Which of the following best represents duties and obligations of government?
questions.explanation: Providing public utilities is a duty of government; the other options are duties of citizens.

questions.topic: Election: types and ingredients of a free and fair election
questions.stem: An electoral process in which candidates for elective offices are selected by party members is known as
questions.explanation: Party members choose their candidates in primary elections.

questions.topic: Election: types and ingredients of a free and fair election
questions.stem: The principle whereby a legislator's tenure is abruptly brought to an end by his constituency is known as
questions.explanation: Recall allows constituents to remove their representative before the end of the term.

questions.stem: One of the main functions of a political party is
questions.explanation: Parties aggregate (combine) diverse interests into policy programmes.

questions.stem: Which of the following traditional Nigerian societies practised the system of checks and balances?
questions.explanation: In the Old Oyo (Yoruba) system the Alaafin, Oyomesi and Ogboni checked one another.

questions.stem: In terms of administrative structure, which of the following sets of pre-colonial Nigerian political systems do NOT match?
questions.explanation: Benin was a centralized kingdom while the Igbo were acephalous; the other pairs share the same structure.

questions.topic: Comparison of British and French colonial administration
questions.stem: Nationalist activities were earlier in British than in French West Africa because the
options: French West Africans were not interested in having self-government
British colonialists were no longer interested in governing their acquired territories
French administrative policies did not allow for political agitation
nationalists in British West Africa were more united than their French counterparts
questions.explanation: French assimilation and repressive policies (e.g. indigénat) stifled political agitation.

questions.stem: In British West Africa, the elective principle was first introduced in
questions.explanation: The Clifford Constitution of 1922 in Nigeria introduced the elective principle (Sierra Leone 1924, Gold Coast 1925).

questions.stem: A thorny issue during the 1957/58 Nigerian constitutional conferences was the
options: leadership of the first post-independence government
control of the Mid-West by the Western Region
questions.explanation: The minorities question led to the Willink Commission of 1957.

questions.stem: In the 1963 Constitution, there was separation of powers between the
options: president and the commander-in-chief of the armed forces
head of state and the president
head of government and the head of state
questions.explanation: The 1963 Constitution separated the ceremonial President (head of state) from the Prime Minister (head of government).

questions.stem: A major feature which differentiated the 1963 and 1979 constitutions was that in the former,
options: ministers were appointed from the National Assembly
ministers were appointed from outside the National Assembly
the prime minister was elected by the whole country
the National Assembly comprised the senate and the House of Assembly
questions.explanation: Under the 1963 parliamentary constitution ministers were members of parliament; under 1979 they came from outside.

questions.topic: The Judiciary (post-independence): structure, functions and workings
questions.stem: A court order compelling the executive or its agencies to produce an unlawfully detained person is called a writ of
questions.explanation: Habeas corpus requires a detained person to be produced before the court.

questions.stem: The primary function of the Armed Forces of Nigeria is to
options: promote and protect the security of the nation
protect the head of state and commander-in-chief of the armed forces of the nation
protect the citizens against corrupt and oppressive politicians
project the country's image by participating in peace-keeping operations
questions.explanation: The constitutional role of the armed forces is defence of the nation's security and territorial integrity.

questions.topic: Public Commissions Established by the 1979 and Subsequent Constitutions
questions.stem: Which organ was enshrined in the 1979 Constitution to protect public servants from political interference and arbitrary dismissal?
questions.explanation: Key printed A; correct answer is D because the Federal Civil Service Commission controls appointment, discipline and dismissal of civil servants, insulating them from politicians.

questions.stem: The political party that replaced NNDP before independence was
questions.explanation: The Nigerian Youth Movement displaced the NNDP as the dominant party in Lagos in the 1938 Legislative Council elections.

questions.stem: Apart from discussing the draft of the 1979 constitution, what was the major pre-occupation of the Constituent Assembly in 1978?
questions.explanation: The proposed Federal Sharia Court of Appeal dominated and almost broke up the 1977/78 Constituent Assembly.

questions.stem: The first minority state to be created in the Nigerian federation was
questions.explanation: The Mid-Western Region was created in 1963.

questions.topic: Problems of Nigerian Federalism and solutions
questions.stem: One major constraint on the smooth operation of federalism in Nigeria is the
options: lack of an acceptable revenue allocation formula
inability to conduct a successful census
questions.explanation: Revenue allocation has been the most persistent source of conflict in Nigerian federalism.

questions.topic: Comparison between public corporations and parastatals
questions.stem: One of the basic differences between ministries and public corporations is that while ministries are
options: run on rules, public corporations are not
wholly owned by the government, public corporations are owned by both government and individuals
not established with specific statutes, public corporations are
not important in developmental process, public corporations are
questions.explanation: Each public corporation is created by its own statute; ministries are not.

questions.stem: Privatization and commercialization of public enterprises in Nigeria will lead to further entrenchment of
questions.explanation: Transferring public enterprises to private owners strengthens capitalism.

questions.stem: The 1976 Local Government Reforms has
options: reduced political corruption at the local level
resulted in accelerated development in the rural areas
created more autonomy for local administration
reduced the political roles of traditional rulers
questions.explanation: The 1976 reforms confined traditional rulers to advisory/ceremonial roles.

questions.stem: The Babangida administration's transition to civil rule programme officially started in
questions.explanation: Key printed D; correct answer is C because the transition programme was announced in 1987 after the Political Bureau report (Babangida took power in August 1985).

questions.stem: A major negative impact of military intervention in Nigerian politics is the
options: domination of the economy by foreign powers
poor performance of the military in foreign peace-keeping operations
neglect of the welfare of military personnel
questions.explanation: Military rule drew officers into politics, eroding professionalism.

questions.stem: The committee that recommended Abuja as the new Federal Capital was headed by
questions.explanation: The 1975 Panel on the Location of the Federal Capital was chaired by Justice Akinola Aguda.

questions.stem: The term, comprador bourgeoisie, has been used by scholars to describe
options: Nigerian businessmen who represent foreign interests
questions.explanation: Comprador bourgeoisie are local businessmen acting as agents of foreign capital.

questions.stem: Which of the following countries is closely associated with the development of Ajaokuta Steel Project?
questions.explanation: Key printed B; correct answer is D because Ajaokuta Steel was designed and built with the Soviet Union (Russia) through Tyazhpromexport.

questions.stem: The foreign affairs minister who advocated the 'Concert of Medium Powers' was
questions.explanation: Bolaji Akinyemi proposed the Concert of Medium Powers in 1987.

questions.stem: Which of the following reasons best explains why Nigeria during the first republic, could not pursue an independent foreign policy?
options: The numerous differences among the ethnic groups
Nigeria's economy was dependent on the Western countries
questions.explanation: Economic dependence on Britain and the West made the Balewa government pro-Western.

questions.stem: The British prime minister who opposed the cancellation of Nigeria's debt was
questions.explanation: Margaret Thatcher's government refused calls to write off Nigeria's debts.

questions.topic: Africa as the “centre piece” of Nigeria’s foreign policy
questions.stem: Which of the following African countries received Nigeria's assistance to fight her war of independence in 1975/76?
questions.explanation: Nigeria backed the MPLA in Angola in 1975/76.

questions.stem: Which Nigerian was the executive secretary of the ECA?
questions.explanation: Adebayo Adedeji headed the UN Economic Commission for Africa (1975-1991).

questions.topic: Africa as the “centre piece” of Nigeria’s foreign policy
questions.stem: Nigeria was regarded as a 'Frontline State' because she
options: assisted liberation struggles in Southern Africa
sent troops for peace-keeping in Somalia
questions.explanation: Nigeria was an honorary Frontline State for its support of liberation movements in Southern Africa.

questions.stem: The major strategy used by OPEC to influence oil price is by
options: determining the quantity of oil to be produced at any given period
influencing buyers at the international market to buy at high price
allowing member countries to produce at their discretion
increasing the supply of the commodity
questions.explanation: OPEC sets production quotas to regulate supply and hence price.

questions.stem: The Gulf War of 1990 is an indication that the U.N.O. is unable to
questions.explanation: The outbreak of the Gulf War showed the UN cannot guarantee permanent peace.

questions.stem: The concept of sovereignty can best be defined as the
options: state of being supreme in authority
questions.explanation: Sovereignty is supreme, final legal authority within a state.

questions.stem: Power is understood to mean the
options: relationship between the government and the people
desire to seize the state apparatus
questions.explanation: Power is the capacity or ability to make others obey; the right to do so is authority.

questions.stem: The institutions which constitute the main organs of the government of a nation are the

questions.stem: A major objective of the public Complaints Commission is

Addressing the grievances of individuals and groups

Reliance on Western donors for funds

Nigeria, Libya, Iraq and Saudi Arabia

Executive and legislative powers are fused
Powers of the three arms of government are merged
The tenure of office of the president is limited

questions.stem: The right of citizens to vote is

questions.topic: Pressure groups: definition, types, functions and modes of operation

Contest elections to serve the people

The fear of domination of minorities

questions.stem: Under the Technical Aid Corps, Nigerian experts are deployed to

The pacific, the Caribbean and Europe

questions.topic: Africa as the “centre piece” of Nigeria’s foreign policy

questions.stem: The main representative body of the United Nations is the

questions.stem: The AU differs from the OAU in having

questions.topic: Public opinion: meaning, formation and measurement

aggregate views of groups on particular government activities
views held by the president of the country
views of the Chief Justice of the country

of the existence of an organized structure in the area
the Europeans ensured that the farmlands of the natives were not confiscated

members of the executive are elected

is not easy to manipulate bills

questions.topic: The Judiciary (post-independence): structure, functions and workings

questions.stem: Unitary system of government, is more suitable to a country
options: with a robust and dynamic economy
with a relatively small area and a homogenous population

Public opinion has dimensions such as substance, orientation (direction) and intensity; polling is a method of measuring it, not a dimension.

questions.stem: The body that is responsible for the appointment discipline, promotion and dismissal of civil servants

ensured good governance of the districts

harshness in trade laws as it concerns the Africans
government's rejection of a demand for an increase of 50 percent in the cost-of-living allowances

Lagos protest against water rate in 1908

questions.stem: The emergence of nationalism was essentially the result of the ills of

questions.stem: The Nigeria Independence Constitution was modified by the

questions.stem: The option A4 model was used in the conduct of the

questions.stem: The granting of asylum to Charles Taylor by Nigeria was to

questions.stem: Commonwealth nations are represented in other member nations by

questions.stem: The maintenance of law and order is a function of the

questions.topic: Election: types and ingredients of a free and fair election

questions.topic: Public opinion: meaning, formation and measurement

questions.explanation: The judiciary interprets laws.

questions.explanation: A party system describes how a country is governed through political parties.

questions.explanation: Political parties seek to win power, while pressure groups only seek to influence government policies.

Appointment of Army officers into political post

duties an individual imposes on himself
duties political parties demand of their registered members

increased the powers of the federal government

furthering the decision on colonialism as previously discussed in the Berlin conference
deciding on how to penetrate Africa for economic adventurism

it was resolved that the Nigerians federation be organized on ethnic basis
it was concluded that a quasi-federal structure should be developed for colonial Nigeria
all unofficial members of the legislative council participated

contest for the federal election of 1964

confirmed Nigeria as a federal structure

questions.topic: Public corporations: definition, types, purpose and functions

questions.stem: The Nigeria-Cameroun crisis over Bakassi Peninsula was subject to the decision of
